item.title: ‘We’re not asking for luxury’: school protesters in Paris suburb feel abandoned by French state
item.author: Angelique Chrisafis in Sevran
item.content:encoded: Students say they are desperate to get back to class but conditions are so bad that the protests must continueOn a normal school day, Mohammed, 17, wakes at 6am, cares for his younger siblings to help his single mother who works as a security guard, then takes two crowded buses and a local train to get to his high school in Sevran, a low-income town in the suburbs north-east of Paris.“There aren’t enough chairs or desks to go round, so some students have to stand up,” Mohammed said. “Classes can be so packed you can’t interact with the teacher. In this year’s heatwaves, it felt like 40 degrees in overcrowded classrooms with no shade or curtains. It was so hot my brain couldn’t function.”Continue reading...

item.title: Yankees news: Should Boone Stay or Should Boone Go
item.author: Nick Power
item.content:encoded: New York Post | Jon Heyman: ($) One of the most prominent names in Yankees media added his voice to the chorus calling for Aaron Boone’s dismissal Friday. The reasons are not revelatory — lack of postseason success, discipline, and accountability. Heyman offers his own “analytics,” namely the Yankees manager’s inability to lead his team to a single championship in nine years (and only one World Series berth as well). He joins a crowded field, including The Athletic’s Ian O’Connor, in drawing a line in the sand.New York Daily News | Gary Phillips: Despite the increasing urgency for a leadership change from journalists and fans alike, there are some key indicators that Boone is likely to stick around for at least one more season. For one, he’s owed $5.5 million for last year, the last on his deal. For another, the impending lockout would make it an uphill battle for a new manager to put in the legwork necessary to build trust with his players before the new season, as they wouldn’t be able to contact each other from December 1st until a new CBA is struck. Boone also retains the vocal support of his locker room, a fact which might solicit eyerolls from the Yankees faithful but still holds sway with the front office.FanGraphs | Brendan Gawlowski: The Arizona Fall League is a full week into play at this point, and Michael Zeno helpfully wrote up the action on how the Yankees’ prospects fared our west during this initial showing. For more on one of said prospects, here’s Gawlowski on a number of different AFL-ers (a-fellers?) who he saw in person. He’s a big fan of Dax Kilby, the Yankees’ top draft pick from 2025 who had an injury-riddled year and is catching up on lost time. Gawlowski wrote that Kilby is the best player he saw, and that he “is quick and direct to the ball, he doesn’t leak early, his swing stays on plane forever, he adjusts well off the fastball, and he can use the whole field.” Good review!MLB Trade Rumors | Charlie Wright: The 2026 season went better for Paul Goldschmidt than his Yankees debut in 2025, when he burned bright early but faded down the stretch. There was some of that this past season as well for the veteran, but he was generally more consistent and the Yankees were more disciplined about using him less against righties. All told, it led to a 111 OPS+ and 18 homers in 380 plate appearances, good for a .452 slugging percentage that was his highest since his NL MVP-winning 2022 in St. Louis (with a reliable glove at first, too). Although Goldschmidt turned 39 in September, he would like to keep playing in 2027.The fit might not be there for the Yankees with Luis García Jr. now joining Ben Rice in the first base mix next spring, but if Goldy wants to play for a few million again, I suspect that someone can pick him up — if not only to see if he can get the 10 homers he needs to reach 400 in an excellent career that is a bit of a dark horse Hall of Fame case.

item.title: As it happened: Attritional 2026 edition of Il Lombardia won with brilliant solo attack
item.author: Stephen Puddicombe
item.content:encoded: Il Lombardia: Paul Seixas puts in stunning solo ride to claim first MonumentFrenchman trailed by Enric Mas, Giulio CicconePaul Seixas (Fra) Decathlon CMA CGMEnric Mas Nicolau (Spa) Movistar TeamGiulio Ciccone (Ita) Lidl-TrekRemco Evenepoel (Bel) Red Bull-Bora-HansgroheBrandon McNulty (USA) UAE Team Emirates-XRGTom Pidcock (GBr) Pinarello-Q36.5 Pro Cycling TeamPello Bilbao Lopez De Armentia (Spa) Bahrain VictoriousChristian Scaroni (Ita) XDS AstanaFilippo Zana (Ita) Soudal-QuickStepMathys Rondel (Fra) Tudor Pro CyclingHello and welcome to the 2026 edition of Il Lombardia! October 10, 2026 – 4:39 AMNo race in the cycling calendar has been dominated by a single man in recent years as Il Lombardia has been by Tadej Pogačar. The Slovenian has won a record-breaking five editions in succession, each year with increasing supremacy. Now, however, that run will come to an end. The defending champion is out injured, and in his absence we are set for a wide-open race.October 10, 2026 – 4:47 AMIt might poetically be known as Race of the Falling Leaves for its autumnal setting, but the conditions today early on are reflecting the grey, grimmer side to this time of year. There are clouds hanging over the peloton as they wait at the start, and a pressing threat of rain, even if things remain dry for not. October 10, 2026 – 4:53 AMToday will be the final day in the career of many big name riders, and the peloton have formed a guard of honour at the start to see them off. October 10, 2026 – 4:59 AMThere are five retirees in total going through the guard of honour - Pello Bilbao, Ion Izagirre, Rudy Molard, Odd Christian Eiking and Bauke Mollema. All have enjoyed storied careers, and will hope to end their careers in style today.October 10, 2026 – 5:05 AMOne rider who didn’t take part in the Guard of Honour was Primož Roglič. There have been rumours that the Slovenian might be on the brink of retirement, and he himself did not rule out. But his absence from the Guard suggests that he has not made a definitive decision to do so. October 10, 2026 – 5:14 AMThe riders have only recently set off from the unofficial start, which was delayed as the peloton staged a protest. Remco Evenepoel explained via microphone to the crowd that they were protesting about recent failures of organisers to protect their safety, in a series of incidents that have been especially shocking since the death of Finlay Tarling. “We want to make the statement to show to the whole world that we cannot keep accepting the act that guys keep getting injured or literally dying”On behalf of the peloton, Evenepoel said that his message to the organisers of this and future races was: !please make sure that we can race safely, and that we can just do what we like to do without being worried about cars and motorbikes…coming onto the course”October 10, 2026 – 5:19 AMAnd they’re off! Bardiani’s Martin Marcellusi is the first man to attack, and he has a lead of ten seconds as no rider made an immediate response to follow himOctober 10, 2026 – 5:24 AMAfter a subdued first few kilometres in which only Marcellusi attacked, the race has now exploded into life. Multiple men have made moves, among them Visma’s Bruno Armirail, who was so strong at the World Championships a fortnight ago. They’ve not been allowed to go clear, and the peloton is all back together. October 10, 2026 – 5:31 AMThe attacks keep coming, and Alessandro Covi leads the race having managed to build a gap. He's fifteen seconds up the road, but plenty of riders are showing an eagerness to join him. October 10, 2026 – 5:36 AMCovi has been caught, but his Jayco teammate Michael Matthews has immediately counter-attacked. That’s a surprising move, as the Australian’s stock in trade is staying in the peloton and surviving hills to sprint from reduced sprints at the finish - as he did at the World two weeks ago, to win the silver medal. That ride proves he’s in great shape, but is this the best way to race for him to stand a chance of another high finish today? Perhaps not, and the Australian did not fully commit to the move, and has been caught by the peloton. October 10, 2026 – 5:45 AMThings had quietened down for a short while, but the attacking has recommenced now that they have started the Selvino climb. Multiple riders have used its lower slopes to try and go clear, but are being chased down by UAE.October 10, 2026 – 5:54 AMHere's the full story of the riders protest at the start of the day. Many also shared the same message on social media as the protest was being made including leader of the CPA Adam Hansen.October 10, 2026 – 5:59 AMFor the first time in a while, there’s a group of riders who have a gap of a few seconds. Michael Leonard, Andrea Mifsud, Johannes Kulset and, most notably, Ben O’Connor (the latest big name Jayco leader after Michael Matthews’ attempt earlier) have ten seconds on the peloton, with 4km of the climb still left to complete. October 10, 2026 – 6:03 AMMaxime Decomble has joined O’Connor, Mifsud, Kulset and Leonard. He should add some serious firepower as this group attempts to establish itself as the day’s break, having massively impressed earlier this week by claiming a breakthrough bronze medal at the European championships time trial. With just 2km left to climb, they're 20 seconds up on the peloton. October 10, 2026 – 6:11 AMA group of chasers have joined the five riders at the front as tey go over the top of the climb, and some very strong riders are present in it - former Lombardia podium finisher Fausto Masnada, along with Tiberi, George Bennett, Leemreize, Martí and Moniquet.That makes for a very strong breakaway group, and not one the peloton will necessarily be happy to let go. Let's see if they try to chase them down on the descent. October 10, 2026 – 6:18 AMThe race is far from settled yet, and there's plenty in the peloton not happy with the situation. Visma-Lease a Bike wanted representation in it, and their man Campanaerts has joined it, along with Lidl's Bernard. And the peloton is only ten seconds adrift, as they continue to descend. October 10, 2026 – 6:26 AMHere was O'Connor, Leonard and Kulset on the climb, three of the riders who instigated the move. The group has since swelled to 14, and their hopes are looking brighter again, building a lead of 50 seconds. It remains a very strong group to allow up the road, however, and there will surely be some trepidation in the peloton. October 10, 2026 – 6:34 AMWith the gap having exceeded one minute for the first time all day, it does not seem as if we have our break of the day. The likes of Visma and Lidl are represented in it, but UAE, Decathlon and Red Bull are not, so it'll be up to them to control it and eventually bring it back. October 10, 2026 – 6:40 AMFor unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews. You'll get comprehensive race coverage, subscriber-exclusive analysis from our expert columnists, in-depth features and industry-leading tech insight. Plus, the Cyclingnews app lets you follow the action wherever you go!October 10, 2026 – 6:50 AMThe riders are climbing again, but in a much calmer way than up the previous hill of Selvino. The peloton is holding the gap at two minutes, and are all together, after world champion Brandon McNulty made his way back into it following a mechanical. October 10, 2026 – 7:03 AMBauke Mollema is riding his thirteenth consecutive Il Lombardia today, and the eighteenth of his career - the eleventh of which, in 2019, he won, making him the only former winner riding today.He was also one of those who went through the morning's Guard of Honour, to mark his retirement. Have a read of our full story on those riders.October 10, 2026 – 7:12 AMThe riders are currently climbing up the Passo di Valcava. This is one of the longest of the day, lasting 10.4km, and rises at a steepish gradient too of 6.1%. But it's being taken on at a steady pace by both break and peloton, between which the gap is holding steady at two minutes. October 10, 2026 – 7:20 AMDecathlon have taken responsibility for leading the peloton, for their leader Paul Seixas, and are being assisted by UAE. The latter have expressed some concerns regarding the fitness of their leader Isaac del Toro ahead of the race, but by contributing to the chase, appear to have confidence in his ability to win this race. October 10, 2026 – 7:29 AMRemco Evenepoel's Red Bull-Bora Hansgrohe team is also contributing to the pace-setting. Evenepoel was in bullish mood going into the race, sounding confidant of his chances of taking what would be a first Lombardia title, and is backing those words up with actions by having his team at the forefront of the race. October 10, 2026 – 7:39 AMThe riders are now descending Valpiana, their lead have decreased a little on it to 1:40. That's four climbs done, but there are still five more to come, with as many kilometres still to ride as many entire races. This is a truly punishing race, that will seriously take its toll. October 10, 2026 – 7:47 AMOne team notable by their absence at the front of the peloton is Pinarello-Q36.5. In Tom Pidcock they have one of the favourites for the win today, and he acknowledged as much going into the race. But compared to the stellar line-ups of UAE, Red Bull and Decathlon, his Pinarello-Q36.5 support is notably weaker. October 10, 2026 – 7:59 AMThe riders are currently travelling through a valley road, a rare section of flat on an otherwise up-and-down parcours, and the break is using it to increase their lead. It's now up to 2:45, the highest it's been all day. October 10, 2026 – 8:09 AMAs promised by the race's nickname, here's some fallen leaves on the roadside. This is one of the most atmospheric races of the season, and thankfully the rain has held off to keep those leaves crisp rather than damp. October 10, 2026 – 8:14 AMEvery one of the last 21 monuments since Liège–Bastogne–Liège 2022 has been won by either Tadej Pogačar, Mathieu van der Poel, or a Belgian. With Pogačar and Van der Poel both not present, the only way that steak will continue is if another Belgian wins today.Remco Evenepoel is probably the favourite for the win, but there are many more non-Belgians in contention. Be sure to have a read of our full run-down before the attacks ignite this race into life.October 10, 2026 – 8:19 AMResplendent in his new European Champion jersey he won in Ljubljana last week, Evenepoel is the favourite for the win. That victory suggests he’s in top form again, and over whatever ailed him at the Worlds road race in Montreal, and the fact he has placed second-place to Pogačar in each of the last two editions (and by a considerable margin, of over a minute ahead of the riders in third place) indicates that he stands to gain most from his absence. October 10, 2026 – 8:26 AMThe gap has grown to over three minutes, but there's an increase in the peloton as they fight for position going on to the fifth climb of the day, Giovenzana. October 10, 2026 – 8:38 AMUAE are setting the pace in the peloton on the climb, with Sivakov setting a tough pace. Though they also have recently-crowned world champion Brandon McNulty in their ranks, you suspect they are working for Del Toro (assuming he's fully fit). This is a huge chance for the young star to take what would be a landmark first monument victory in his career, before he turns 23 next month, having already this season made the podium at Strade Bianche and won GP de Montreal.October 10, 2026 – 8:43 AMUAE's pace has slashed the gap to the leaders back down to 2:15. O'Connor responded by upping the pace in the break, and looks stronger than the rest, but isn't pushing on too hard in other to keep the group together as they reach the top of the climb. October 10, 2026 – 8:51 AMIs Paul Seixas ready to take the first monument win of his fledgling career? After breaking through with a seventh place finish here last year, the Frenchman went from strength to strength, but is without a victory since his first classics triumph at La Flèche Wallonne in April, and was unfortunate to fall out of contention late on during the Worlds with cramps. The previously feverish expectations have tempered a little as a result, but being able to go under the radar might give him the advantage he needs to win what might turn out to be a tactical finale. October 10, 2026 – 8:57 AMCohesion is breaking down in the break, which has split into three different groups. Panic seems to have set in after the last climb saw their gap so reduced, although it has increased a little again, up to 2:30.It appears as though the break will reform, but the action suggests hostilities will ignite come the upcoming climb - the famous Madonna del Ghisallo. October 10, 2026 – 9:06 AMSubscribe to Cyclingnews for comprehensive race coverage of the UCI Gravel World Championships, alongside the final Monument of the season, Il Lombardia. Subscribers get unlimited access to exclusive analysis from our expert columnists, in-depth features and industry-leading tech insight. Plus, the Cyclingnews app lets you follow the action wherever you go!October 10, 2026 – 9:15 AMIt will be fascinating to see how Brandon McNulty goes today. Though he’s now the world champion, Isaac del Toro still pulls rank in UAE’s line-up; but at the same time, McNulty could benefit from the strength of his team’s numbers with the kind of surprise attack that saw him take the gold medal in Montreal, if given freedom to do so. Everyone will now know that his is not a wheel they can afford to let go.October 10, 2026 – 9:21 AMAmong some of the outside bets for the victory today are Matteo Jorgenson and Ben Helay, pictured in the peloton here. Healy will surely attack at some point, as he seems to in every race he competes in, and if he can time it right then he has a chance in a parcours that should suit him. And Jorgenson looked in brilliant form riding for the USA at the Worlds, and should now get a chance to ride as a leader for Visma-Lease a Bike; albeit alongside another in-for contender, Giro dell'Emilia winner Davide Piganzoli.October 10, 2026 – 9:25 AMRace on! We're on the famous Madonna del Ghisallo, and the tension is up in the peloton as they rise to what is one of the most important moments of the race. EF lead them onto the climb, just over two minutes after the break started it. Will we see any attacks on it?October 10, 2026 – 9:30 AMThere have been no attacks yet in the peloton, as UAE take control with Jan Christen. By contrast the break has split into pieces, with O'Connor going clear with Leonard, and everyone else distanced. October 10, 2026 – 9:35 AMEF are clearly in an ambitious mood today. They've put Juan Felipe Rodriguez at the front of the peloton, and is setting a fast pace enough to drop multiple rides - including the UAE domestiques Christen and Großschartner who had been leading the peloton.And as we speak the pace is up again, as Red Bull take over from Rodriguez and EF with Giulio Pellizzari. October 10, 2026 – 9:40 AMO'Connor and Leonard have been joined again by 6 of the riders dropped earlier on the climb, as they come to 1.5km from the summit - Bennett, Leemreize, Moniquet, Masnada, Bernard and Vervaeke. October 10, 2026 – 9:41 AMWe have our first attack from the peloton, and it's Visma's Jorgenson! He's being marked by some of the same American compatriots who he worked so well with in Montreal, albeit now as rivals - Lidl's Simmons and UAE's McNulty, plus Italy and Astana's Scaroni. October 10, 2026 – 9:46 AMThe American-flavoured quarter have crested the climb, just 45 seconds after the breakaway group, and a handful of seconds ahead of the peloton, which is being led by Red Bull's Pellizzari. Remco Evenepoel will be grateful that he still has teammates to help him now the attacks have come, although another, Primož Roglič, was struggling to hang on over the top. October 10, 2026 – 9:54 AMWe're entering the finale of this race now, as they approach the finishing circuit, with just three climbs left. Simmons, McNulty, Jorgenson and Scaroni have rolled the dice and made their move, and are committed to it, Behind, Red Bull are chasing, and keeping them well in check, at 12 seconds. Meanwhile the seven riders remain from the day's break are retaining a lead of 45 seconds over the chasers. October 10, 2026 – 10:00 AMThe McNulty group has been caught by the peloton, Red Bull having successfully controlled it. That's the first big test of the day passed by the team, but they are sure to come under more pressure as rivals don't wait for Evenepoel to make his move. October 10, 2026 – 10:05 AMIt's still Giulio Pellizzari who leads the peloton for Red Bull, but Evenepoel has reinforcements now as Roglič has made his way back into the group. He's riding tempo for now, keeping the break at just under a minute, and discouraging any more attacks - but that's likely to change when they hit the net climb, which will be a first ascent of San Fermo della Battaglia.October 10, 2026 – 10:13 AMIt's still been Pellizzari who has been leading the peloton, and he's clearly tiring, with the break's lead growing to 1:20. But as they enter the final circuit there's a big fight for position as other teams come to the fore, notably Netcompany and Visma, the latter of which still looks very well-represented in the group with five riders. October 10, 2026 – 10:18 AMThe break are just about to begin San Fermo della Battaglia for the first time, with a lead of 1:30 over the peloton - which, though still made up of dozens of riders, will surely be a lot smaller by the time they reach the top.October 10, 2026 – 10:22 AMPellizzari has resumed control on the climb, and this time has Evenepoel right on his wheel. The other favourites have all massed towards the front to be near his wheel, attentive no doubt of a possible attack from the Belgian...October 10, 2026 – 10:26 AMPellizzari leads the peloton over the climb, with not much more than 20 riders left on his wheel. 45 seconds is now the gap to them and the break, which is down to 6 riders with Leemreize dropped on the climb.October 10, 2026 – 10:29 AMPellizzari led Evenepoel up the last climb; will Red Bull manage to maintain that same control up the more difficult Civiglio, which the riders are set to begin in a few moments? Brace yourselves - in the past this has been where Il Lombardia has been decided, and the same could well be the case today. October 10, 2026 – 10:33 AMJorgenson was dropped on the previous climb, but has made his way back into the peloton and leads it as they begin the climb of Civiglio, now just 40 seconds behind the 6 remaining riders from the break.He doesn't last long, however, and UAE take control from him. October 10, 2026 – 10:36 AMYates leads for UAE, followed by his teammates McNulty and Del Toro; then Seixas, Healy and Pidcock, plus around 15 other riders. Meanwhile Healy's teammate Leonard has dropped everyone else in the break, and now leads the race. October 10, 2026 – 10:38 AMSeixas takes over at the front and has upped the pace, and has caught all the riders from the break.He's also reduced the group to about ten riders - and Evenepoel is one of those being dropped!October 10, 2026 – 10:39 AMSeixas is on the charge! Only two riders can keep up with him - Pidcock and Ciccone. Mas is fourth on the road chasing behind, and Del Toro further behind. October 10, 2026 – 10:41 AMWell, it's not exactly an attack, but Seixas has ridden Pidcock and Ciccone off his wheel with his relentless pace and now leads the race by himself! October 10, 2026 – 10:46 AMSeixas crests the Civiglio in the lead of the race, about 30 seconds ahead of Ciccone, who has been joined by Mas, and about 45 seconds ahead of Pidcock, who was dropped and has been joined by Zana.Then comes a group containing McNulty, Healy, Widar and Onley, while Evenepoel and Del Toro are even further adrift, at over a minute. October 10, 2026 – 10:50 AMThis is far from over yet. Seixas doesn't look overly confidant on the descent, while Ciccone is setting the pace behind with Mas in toe, and reducing the gap. It's at about 20 seconds. October 10, 2026 – 10:54 AMSeixas might not have been so comfortable on the descent, but he sure was on the flat section, where he managed to increase his lead to Ciccone and Mas to 35 seconds. He's now swung onto the final climb of the race - will he tire, or does he have enough in reserve to finish this off?October 10, 2026 – 10:59 AMMas has attacked Ciccone on the climb, and dropped him. But it might be too little too late in term of the race win, as Seixas is now 43 seconds ahead. October 10, 2026 – 11:03 AMThe moment Seixas dropped Ciccone on Civiglio to go clear at the front of the race. He's since grown his lead at the front to 50 seconds on Mas in second, with just 3km left to ride, while Ciccone is now at risk of losing a spot on the podium as a chase group being led by Pidcock bares down on him. October 10, 2026 – 11:04 AMSeixas flies under the flamme rouge, poised to take the biggest win of his fledgling career so far, with nobody within 45 seconds of him.October 10, 2026 – 11:06 AMThe 20-year-old savours the moment and crosses the line with his hands in the air - the first ever monument win of his career!Behind, Mas holds on for a very impressive and for many unexpected second place, continuing his superb end to this season, while Ciccone also manages to hang on to the final place on the podium.October 10, 2026 – 11:11 AMPaul Seixas (Fra) Decathlon CMA CGMEnric Mas Nicolau (Spa) Movistar TeamGiulio Ciccone (Ita) Lidl-TrekRemco Evenepoel (Bel) Red Bull-Bora-HansgroheBrandon McNulty (USA) UAE Team Emirates-XRGTom Pidcock (GBr) Pinarello-Q36.5 Pro Cycling TeamPello Bilbao Lopez De Armentia (Spa) Bahrain VictoriousChristian Scaroni (Ita) XDS AstanaFilippo Zana (Ita) Soudal-QuickStepMathys Rondel (Fra) Tudor Pro CyclingOctober 10, 2026 – 11:15 AMToday's historic winner, the 20-year-old Paul Seixas. You sense we will get very used to this image of him celebrating at the finish.October 10, 2026 – 11:20 AMThe king is dead; long live the king. Tadej Pogačar might have had to miss this race due to injury, but his heir apparent Paul Seixas won the race in a manner he would have been proud of. We’ve expected it for some time now, but this result further suggests that Seixas is on course to inherit Pogačar’s status as the best rider in the peloton. October 10, 2026 – 11:22 AM"Everything went perfect. The teammates [did a] great, awesome job. Everyone pushed more than what they had to do… I had amazing legs."I had the feeling that today was a great day, and I managed to make the difference at the moment I chose, maybe a bit earlier, because I felt like the rhythm was not high enough at the start of the climb – for me at least – to make the difference, so I had to accelerate early, maybe a bit too early. There were some not really steep parts, so I had to manage my efforts and accelerate in the hard parts."Then I did the best I could, a TT, me against myself and yeah, it was crazy."October 10, 2026 – 11:31 AMWhile Seixas takes the headlines and glory, it has also been another great day for Enric Mas. After winning the Vuelta a España, it was unclear whether he still had the form or the will to still race competitively in the final weeks of the season, and it did indeed appear as though he was winding down, abandoning the World Championships on his first race day after that historic result. But today he showed that same form that brought him success in Spain, and he makes the podium of Il Lombardia for the second time in his career, having also placed second in 2022, behind Tadej Pogačar. October 10, 2026 – 11:40 AMCompleting the podium is Giulio Ciccone, who continued his fine (albeit winless) run of form with third-place, repeating his finish here from two years ago, in what it has been announced will be his final race for Lidl-Trek.Based on his reaction upon crossing the line, it's a result Ciccone is happy with. And it also makes it a third year in a row in which he has made the podium of a monument - something that only Pogačar, Van der Poel and Evenepoel have also done in that time.October 10, 2026 – 11:58 AMThanks for joining us today, and indeed for the whole season. It’s been a real roller-coaster of a season, with thrilling racing, records broken by all-time greats, plus the occasional shocking result - and now ends with the crowning of the sport’s next superstar, Paul Seixas. It’s been a pleasure reporting on it.That’s it for the major road races of 2026, but it’s still a busy time in the world of cycling in terms of transfers, news and other disciplines beyond the road. Be sure to keep updated with Cyclingnews!

item.title: Matt Beers ready to chase 'a medal of any kind' as he picks shot at Gravel World Championships glory over Life Time Grand Prix
item.author: simone.giuliani@futurenet.com (Simone Giuliani)
item.content:encoded: When we asked Matt Beers what he still wanted to achieve in his career, there was no hesitation: "A World Championship medal is the one thing that had alluded me'. The UCI Gravel World Championships in Nannup has provided the perfect opportunity for the gravel rider and mountain biker to change that.The South African hasn't been a regular at the UCI Gravel World Championships, which is usually dominated at the pointy end by road riders, last riding the event in the opening year of 2022 and instead keeping his focus on the Life Time Grand Prix. This year, though, offered a compelling reason to change course, not just for Beers but in fact for the whole Specialized Off-Road team who had mapped out attending the race in Western Australia at the start of the season. So Beers made the trip, with a couple of weeks pre-race to get settled, a support team, plus fellow Life Time competitors and leaders Keegan Swenson and Sofia Gomez Villafañe, and European-based Mads Würtz Schmidt and Geerike Schreurs. "Australia is kind of a level playing field for everyone," Beers told at the Specialized team's Nannup base, a peaceful abode just out of town where they were relaxing after having been out riding the final loop. "We all have to deal with jet lag, we all have to deal with the travel, the terrain is different to everyone, besides obviously the Australians with local knowledge, but I think that it really does level it out for the Europeans and the US riders, or myself as a South African, because you're always stronger on home turf. It's the same food, the climate," said Beers, adding that there was also that he had never been to Australia and "it looked awesome". And Beers has committed fully to the task. Most of his fellow Life Time Grand Prix competitors at the race were using Little Sugar MTB as their one permitted drop round for the six-race series, Beers however decided to give the prior Chequamegon a miss as well, which meant he was out of the series which for many years has been a core of his season, along with the Cape Epic which he has won four times."I decided I had make a call on the Grand Prix, just because of travel and it was kind of 'Should I just be average at everything, or really put focus on the World Champs and try my best on a course that I think I can do quite well at'," said Beers. "And I chose that path. Whether it's the right one, we don't know. We'll see. But that's the bed I've made."You could question both ways of doing it, if I decided to do Life Time, I would maybe be like, 'Oh man, I could have had a World Champ by now'... I don't know, it can kind of be both ways."However, with the decision made and the Life Time Grand Prix now waiting for next year, Sunday will be the arbiter when he lines up in the kit of South Africa on a course that is 85% gravel and 144km long with 3,713m of vertical gain.Not riding for, nor againstIt's a race that in many ways Beers says favour his style, with smaller numbers and no "crazy bunches" to deal with as the rider chases his target of a "medal of any kind", but what about all the climbing?"It's a lot of climbing, but it's the kind of climbing I'm used to – five to eight minutes is the longest climb," said Beers. "I would say it's very mountain bike-esque, just the way the terrain is ... It's not climbing where it's accumulated in two climbs. It's just multiple. "It's going to be hard on the longer climbs for me to hang on to the little 60 kilo whippets. But eight minutes, I would say, is kind of my max of what I can hang on. So I'm quite confident that I'll be able to follow most of the moves if I ride smart."This year has been another strong one for Beers, who as well as winning at Cape Epic with partner Tristan Nortje, has come second at Unbound and third at The Traka, while also being an extraordinarily valuable teammate for winner Würtz Schmidt. Even though it is Specialized Off-Road that is supporting the team riders to come out to this race, and it lines up with three key favourites in Beers, Swenson and Würtz Schmidt, the reality on Sunday is that they will all be wearing different jerseys – those of South Africa, the United States and Denmark. How does that work on the gravel roads of the Blackwood Valley as all three chase a world title?"I guess we don't really know, but I mean for sure, we're not going to ride for each other, but we're also not going to ruin each other's chances per se," said Beers. "If Mads or Keegan is off the front, I'm not going to sit on the front and pull them back."Subscribe to Cyclingnews for comprehensive race coverage of the UCI Gravel World Championships, alongside the final Monument of the season, Il Lombardia. item.title: 'A lot of eyes have been on me and I need to learn how to deal with that' – Tom Pidcock adjusts to favourite status ahead of Il Lombardia
item.author: Patrick Fletcher
item.content:encoded: Tom Pidcock has been one of the strongest riders of the past couple of weeks, and the question of whether he can win Il Lombardia is perhaps not a question of legs but of tactics. The Pinarello-Q36.5 rider kicked off his late-season one-day campaign with victory at the GP Industria & Artigianato, but since then he has suffered a string of near misses, at the GP de Québec (4th), GP de Montréal (6th), World Championships (7th), Giro dell’Emilia (2nd), and Tre Valli Varesine (2nd). "I like to think so, but I made a few mistakes the last week," Pidcock, speaking at the Il Lombardia teams presentation in Bergamo on Friday evening, said in relation to his usually-sharp ability to read a race. "I think it’ll be a bit of tactical game. Maybe some energy for the end will be important."As for what those mistakes were and the lessons he’s learned, he added: "I think that I have stronger legs than perhaps I thought. And sometimes, I just need to control the race myself and not rely on others."Pidcock, in some ways, has already done just that. In fact, over the past couple of weeks he has established himself as arguably the most honest, and dare we say generous, rider in action right now. At the World Championships he was arguably the most committed rider in the group that was dithering so dramatically behind the lone leader Brandon McNulty. A few days ago, at the Giro dell’Emilia, he led the chase of Davide Piganzoli on his own in the final kilometre, burning riders off his wheel and not caring that Oscar Onley was still sucking it. And when Matteo Jorgenson initially refused to pull through in the winning move at Tre Valli Varesine, he made his exasperation abundantly clear. "I think a lot of eyes have been on me in last races and I need to learn how to deal with that sometimes," Pidcock said in Bergamo. "It’s not easy. But yeah, it’s also a sign of respect, that guys think I’m strong enough to ride like that."Pidcock’s season won’t end at Il Lombardia – he’s off to the Tour of Guangxi stage race next week – but it’s the final big objective of what has been a busy year that has seen him win a World Championship title on the mountain bike in the middle of his road season."I definitely feel it’s been a long year but I feel good at the same time," he said."I’ve been listening to my body quite well, taking the rest where I need it, and I think the result is that I’m in great shape now and hopefully I can make the most of it."Subscribe to Cyclingnews for comprehensive race coverage of the UCI Gravel World Championships, alongside the final Monument of the season, Il Lombardia. item.title: Marquez takes MotoGP points lead after Aprilia implosion
item.author: Valentin Khorounzhiy
item.content:encoded: Marc Marquez took an unlikely victory in the Indonesian Grand Prix sprint race after a first-corner incident took out two other victory contenders and a series of problems for title rival Jorge Martin.Martin appeared to be coasting to victory but had to cede position to Marquez and then made a mistake that dropped him off the podium.With Fabio Di Giannantonio attacking for the lead into Turn 1 on the inside and Marquez trying to squeeze in between the VR46 rider and the Aprilias of Marco Bezzecchi and Raul Fernandez, it was close to a four-wide situation at the start - and it ended in disaster for half of the participants.With Di Giannantonio taking a late-braking Marquez wide, Bezzecchi picked up the bike and ended up making contact with Fernandez on the outside, both going down as a result.That first-corner dynamic meant Martin waltzed past, with sudden open road in front of him, to take the lead - and over the first few laps he stretched out a lead of over a second back to Marquez.But he then slowed suddenly to deliberately wave Marquez back through, in what was presumably a bid to artificially raise his front tyre pressure and avoid a penalty for non-compliance.This would tally, as Martin and his crew may have set his tyre pressures expecting to run in traffic, but instead he was into the lead from Turn 1.Once Marquez was handed the lead, Martin quickly pushed back up towards him but struggled to line up any kind of move - and ran off-track on the penultimate lap to relegate himself to fourth place.Instead, Ai Ogura and Di Giannantonio completed the podium.It means Marquez now leads Martin by four points in the standings, with Bezzecchi 59 off the lead after his retirement.Alex Marquez, Pedro Acosta, Fermin Aldeguer, Pecco Bagnaia and Fabio Quartararo rounded out the points - Acosta having served a long-lap penalty for track limits that dropped him from fifth and in-between the Gresini riders.1 Marc Marquez (Ducati) +0.000s2 Ai Ogura (Trackhouse Aprilia) +0.509s3 Fabio Di Giannantonio (VR46 Ducati) +0.835s4 Jorge Martin (Aprilia) +1.947s5 Alex Marquez (Gresini Ducati) +3.410s6 Pedro Acosta (KTM) +5.478s7 Fermin Aldeguer (Gresini Ducati) +7.036s8 Fabio Bagnaia (Ducati) +10.039s9 Fabio Quartararo (Yamaha) +10.248s10 Alex Rins (Yamaha) +13.288s11 Enea Bastianini (Tech3 KTM) +16.834s12 Johann Zarco (LCR Honda) +17.646s13 Jack Miller (Pramac Yamaha) +18.285s14 Luca Marini (Honda) +18.956s15 Brad Binder (KTM) +19.227s16 Diogo Moreira (LCR Honda) +19.293s17 Franco Morbidelli (VR46 Ducati) +19.562s18 Maverick Vinales (Tech3 KTM) +23.472s19 Toprak Razgatlioglu (Pramac Yamaha) +23.834s20 Aleix Espargaro (Honda) +38.336s21 Marco Bezzecchi (Aprilia) DNF22 Raul Fernandez (Trackhouse Aprilia) DNF

item.title: Gravel World Championships: Marianne Vos solos to another rainbow jersey after Rosa Klöser crashes in finale of elite women's race
item.author: Lyne Lamoureux
item.content:encoded: Marianne Vos (Netherlands) made history on Saturday, becoming the first rider to win a second elite women’s gravel world title with a solo victory at the UCI Gravel World Championships in Nannup, Western Australia. The victory brought Vos’ tally to 15 rainbow jerseys across four disciplines: eight in cyclo-cross, two in gravel, plus world titles on the road and track.After rolling with Rosa Klöser (Germany) for 21km, Vos launched a powerful attack in the final 4km in an attempt to drop the German. Klöser fought hard to regain her wheel, but she slid out after hitting a rut on the right-hand side of the road and watched the rainbow jersey ride away from her.Vos and Klöser broke away from a lead group that had fluctuated in size throughout the race. Both had remained in contention as the front group dwindled to three riders before swelling again, with their attack coming after Sofia Gomez Villafañe (Argentina) and Tiffany Cromwell (Australia) each made impressive efforts to chase back to the leaders.Getting back up quickly after her crash, Klöser crossed the line 27 seconds down to take second place, and immediately congratulated Vos.Larissa Hartog (Netherlands) outsprinted Nele Laing (Germany) to take third place, making it two Dutch riders on the podium.With 16 riders in the field, just one fewer than the host nation, the Dutch squad went to the front at the start, and consistently maintained at least two riders in all the splits at the front until the finale.Vos, 39, seemed to be at a loss for words when asked what the win meant to her, simply answering "A lot. Yeah, a lot.""It was more muddy than expected, actually. We had to be careful and some really slippery parts. And Rosa was really, really strong, so on the uphills I had to dig deep to follow," she said."I knew that that final corner around the top and then the descent were going to be tricky, so I wanted to be in front and take them my own lines. But of course it's unfortunate that Rosa crashed there."I was really happy when the World Championships were announced here, and it's a fantastic course here in Western Australia, and it's great to take the rainbow jersey."For the fifth edition of the 2026 UCI Gravel World Championships, the elite women faced a 125.6km course with 3,179m of climbing centred around Nannup, Western Australia. With 85% of the route on gravel, the demanding course wound through the Blackwood Valley, pine plantations, rolling farmland and forested terrain before returning to the off-road cycling hub of Nannup.51 riders took the start in chilly conditions, with temperatures forecast to reach a maximum of 16°C. Overnight rain had compacted the gravel roads, which helped reduce the slipperiness of the pea gravel.Australia’s Ella Bloor made the first move, attacking after 3km with no reaction from the pack, still massed together, and rode on the opening paved section. After giving a few looks over her shoulders, Bloor has a 50-second lead as she hit the first muddy gravel section lined with puddles, 6km later.As the sun peeked through the clouds, the first climb of the day, 5.4km Killarney Rd, caused the first selection, with around 12 riders shelled off the back of the Dutch-led pack. Bloor was reeled in with 105km to go.A puncture for one of the pre-race favourites, Rosa Klöser, forced the German to stop to fix her tyre, and after spending minutes working on her sealant, she had a long solo chase on the horizon to the peloton, down to 25 riders.Sophie Wright (Great Britain) upped the pace on the approach to Brockman Farm, with more riders being shelled off the back on the 2.4km climb with an 8.2% average gradient, as Klöser made her way through dropped riders to reconnect with the 15-rider lead group with 96km to go.The lead group continued to whittle down, now at 10 riders, including the four Dutch riders Marianne Vos, Geerike Schreurs, Elisa Serné and Larissa Hartog. Also making the split were Nicole Frain (Australia), Sofia Gomez Villafañe (Argentina), Erica Magnaldi (Italy), Irina Lützelschwab (Switzerland), Nele Laing (Germany), Ashleigh Moolman-Pasio (South Africa) and Klöser. One rider who was not able to follow the pace was Wendy Oosterwood (Netherlands), winner of the 2026 Gravelking UCI Gravel World Series.Staying on the undulating high roads after the climb, Klöser put in a little dig to try and reduce the Dutch number in the lead group. Behind, the chase group included Oosterwood, Wright, Tiffany Cromwell (Australia), Carolin Schiff (Germany), Maria Laurie (New Zealand), Haley Smith (Canada), Flora Johnson (Great Britain), Janni Spangsberg (Denmark), Joyce Vanderbeken (Belgium) sped down the descent and on flat roads and reconnected with the lead group with 84km to go.Cromwell then attacked solo, dug deep to get a small gap as a heavily marked Vos gave up on chasing her twice, as the Australian gravel champion yo-yoed off the front, but not giving up, she slowly built up her gap.Behind, inside of 73km to go, Schreurs and Moolman-Pasio went off the road on a descent, with the Dutch rider receiving medical attention after the hard crash.As the rain fell, Cromwell’s 1:09 advantage evaporated on the Ellis Creek Climb (2km at 9.1%), where Vos, Laing and Klöser caught her with 500 metres remaining to the summit. The tough ascent had shattered the group, but Hartog and Magnaldi trailing by 22 seconds, and Gomez Villafañe was down two minutes, with the other riders scattered in between.With around 57km to go, Magnaldi and Hartog bridged back to the leaders, swelling the front group to five riders: two Germans, two Dutch and one Italian.The lead group worked well together, although Vos skipped a few turns to take on some gels. On the wide roads, they passed age-group competitors, some of whom tried to briefly latch onto the group.With 40km to go, the chase group of Frain, Lützelschwab and Serne clawed their way back to the front, with Cromwell dangling solo behind on Glacier Climb (3.8km at 3.1%).Hartog got a small gap on the descent, with her Dutch teammates sitting on, leaving the others to do the chasing while Frain countered on a paved section. Vos and Laing reacted immediately with 32km to go, but Magnaldi shut the move down as the pace increased.With three Dutch and two German riders among the eight leaders, riders were watching each other as the pace eased with 28km to go. Meanwhile, Gomez Villafañe, with a new front wheel on her bike, made an impressive chase to the front group after losing two minutes on an earlier climb.Cromwell caught back on and immediately attacked again in the final race of her career with 25km to go, and got big cheers from the fans lining the feed zone as she weaved her way through the age-group riders as she tackled Folly Climb (2.4km at 4.8%).With Vos on her wheel, Klöser jumped from the group to chase down Cromwell. Laing tried to follow but could not keep up with the pace. The duo had a 37-second lead on Laing and Hartog as they crested the climb with 20km to go.The pair worked well together, increasing their lead to over one minute with 7km to go.With 4km to go, sitting on her rival’s wheel, Vos tightened her shoes and put in a massive acceleration. Klöser managed to get back on her wheel, but then slid out and hit the deck, and was out of contention for the victory, allowing Vos to solo away to the rainbow jersey.Marianne Vos (Netherlands)Larissa Hartog (Netherlands)Sofia Gomez Villafane (Argentina)Irina Luetzelschwab (Switzerland)Tiffany Cromwell (Australia)Elisa Serné (Netherlands)Wendy Oosterwoud (Netherlands)Maria Laurie (New Zealand)Joyce Vanderbeken (Belgium)Janni Spangsberg (Denmark)Sophie Wright (Great Britain)Kaitlyn Rauwerda (Canada)Elizabeth Hermolle (Great Britain)Jade Treffeisen (Germany)Flora Johnson (Great Britain)Madeleine Nutt (Great Britain)Theresa Rindler-Bachl (Austria)Karoline Risager Schmidt (Denmark)Victoria Rose Channing Barry (Australia)Anet Barrera Esparza (Mexico)Hayley Simmonds (Great Britain)Laetitia Bilodeau (Canada)Shuwei Hsu (Chinese Taipei)Andrea Loza Fiol (Mexico)Geerike Schreurs (Netherlands)Àshleigh Moolman-Pasio (South Africa)Sharlotte Lucas (New Zealand)Pamela Martino (Argentina)Tessa Neefjes (Netherlands)Riejanne Markus (Netherlands)Valentina Ovalle Calero (Colombia)Michaela Rogan (New Zealand)Shagne Paula Yaoyao (Philippines)Althea Mae Campaña (Philippines)Subscribe to Cyclingnews for comprehensive race coverage of the UCI Gravel World Championships, alongside the final Monument of the season, Il Lombardia. item.title: Tour of Chongming Island: Lorena Wiebes makes it two from two despite electric challenge from Lara Gillespie on stage 2
item.author: Matilda Price
item.content:encoded: Race leader Lorena Wiebes (SD Worx-Protime) sprinted to a second win in as many days on stage 2 of the Tour of Chongming Island, navigating a hectic sprint to power to the victory in the yellow jersey.It wasn't quite a large winning margin that Wiebes is used to, as she had to find her way out of a box and then sprint shoulder-to-shoulder with Lara Gillespie (UAE Team L'Imad) who could match her speed, but just narrowly missed out at the line, settling from second.From the pack sprinting behind, Maggie Coles-Lyster (Human Powered Health) came through for third in front of Clara Copponi (Lidl-Trek).Despite the day's flat profile, there were plenty of attacks in the final 50km with teams desperate to try to find a way to prevent Wiebes from just sweeping this race. A particularly strong group got a gap into the final 30km, including Femke Markus and Femke Markus from SD Worx-Protime, but the peloton were motivated for another sprint and reeled them back in with 15km to go, setting things up for another sprint."It was a day full of breakaway attempts, but we were always well represented and in control of the race," SD Worx-Protime sports director Christian Kos said."Midway through the stage, a dangerous breakaway went clear, but with Femke Gerritse and Femke Markus we had two riders up front. It didn’t guarantee that we would keep the yellow jersey, but it did put us in a very comfortable position. If the breakaway was caught, we could sprint for the stage win with Lorena Wiebes and keep the yellow jersey. If the break stayed away, we had a fresh Femke Gerritse who could go for the stage victory herself. With fifteen kilometers to go, everything came back together."Winning both the stages so far, WIebes continues to lead the general classification, and with another pancake-flat stage to come on stage 3, she may well take a clean sweep of wins in China."It was another great day. Of course, we want to secure the overall victory tomorrow," Kos said.Subscribe to Cyclingnews for comprehensive race coverage of the UCI Gravel World Championships, alongside the final Monument of the season, Il Lombardia. item.title: ‘Like a drill going into my eye’: why the mystery over Havana syndrome refuses to die
item.author: Shaun Walker
item.content:encoded: Dozens of CIA officers have been afflicted by debilitating symptoms over the past decade. Are they the result of ‘mass hysteria’? Or are they from attacks with an energy weapon and, if so, who is responsible? And has there been a cover-up?Shortly after 1am one night in April 2019, a CIA officer on a work trip to London was jolted awake in his hotel room by the most intense head pain he had ever experienced. His body was soaked with sweat and he felt like his eyes were spinning in their sockets. He manoeuvred his way out of bed, hoping to make it to the bathroom to vomit, but found his sense of balance had deserted him. Eventually, he fell back into a fitful, shallow sleep.The next day, arriving at the work meeting he had travelled for, the officer found he could not remember the names of colleagues in the room, people he knew well. As the meeting got under way, he could barely follow the discussion. Initially, he chalked it up to a terrible – if rather odd – case of food poisoning. But over subsequent weeks, worrying symptoms persisted: brain fog, loss of balance and increasingly harsh tinnitus.Continue reading...

item.title: Knicks’ announcement means bad news for everybody, including New York
item.author: Kento Kato
item.content:encoded: While the Knicks and their fans have spent much of the summer celebrating their first championship in 53 years, the upcoming contract situations of a few players have loomed over their heads. And if said players wanted to secure their futures before the start of the season, they were in for a good dose of bad news on Friday.Karl-Anthony Towns, Josh Hart, Miles McBride, and Tyler Kolek all are extension eligible. Hart was asked about his future at the start of training camp and left the door open to anything. Towns and his on going negotiation’s progress, or lack thereof, have taken over the news lately. And for good reason.Many still believe that the two sides will eventually come together for a deal. But the fact that they are reportedly not even close is a bit concerning. Towns, as was on full display during the team’s championship run, is an incredibly pivotal part of the Knicks’ success. Losing him would be devastating, as his shooting gravity and playmaking would be extremely difficult to replace. As if not being able to extend Town wasn’t bad enough, though, the Knicks don’t seem close at all to really extending any of the other players as well. And according to the Knicks themselves, it will remain that way for the foreseeable future.We’ve all seen players make statements about how they want to hold off contract talks when the season begins because they want to focus solely on the upcoming season. But in a rare move, the Knicks were the ones to get ahead of the news and release an official . “As an organization, our entire focus is on preparing for the upcoming season and delivering another year for our fans to be proud of,” a spokesperson from the Knicks said. “As a result, we will not be negotiating contract extensions until later in the season and will remain solely focused on preparing for the start of the season.”Again, it’s rare for a team to be the one to make this statement. And it’s a bit frightening for fans knowing that such important pieces of the core’s future remain largely unknown. One would like to believe that between Towns’, Hart’s, and McBride’s significance to the club and their desire to stay a Knick, we’d have some clearer answers by now.The second apron continues to loom large, so it’s understandable, realistic, and arguably smarter not to extend all three. McBride, unfortunately, was likely playing his last season here regardless of how these extensions went. But to potentially have a future where all, or at least more than one of them, aren’t Knicks would quickly lower the ceiling of this team. The Knicks still would have a core of Jalen Brunson, Mikal Bridges, and OG Anunoby, along with Jose Alvarado, Landry Shamet, and Mohamed Diawara. But the Knicks are a significantly worse team without Towns and, to a lesser degree, without Hart and McBride.It’s not time for full-on panic. Things like this have happened in the past with other negotiations, with everything eventually working out. It could also just be a leverage move. And the most important part is, all parties involved want to extend the marriage.All that being said, it is hard to deny just how ominous of a start this is for a franchise coming off its highest of highs and looking to become the first team to win back-to-back championships for the first time in 53 years.

item.title: As it happened: Late crash sees Dutch dominance continue in women's UCI Gravel World Championships on muddy course
item.author: Tim Bonville-Ginn
item.content:encoded: Marianne Vos went solo over the top of the final climb with Rosa Klöser crashing as she tried to follow. Larissa Hartop outsprinted Nele Laing to take bronze. 1. Marianne Vos (NED) 4:30'04"2. Rosa Klöser (GER) +27"3. Larissa Hartog (NED) +2'15"4. Nele Laing (GER) S.T.5. Erica Magnaldi (ITA) +4'17"6. Sofía Gómez Villafañe (ARG) +5'15"7. Irina Lützelschwab (SWI) +5'28"8. Tiffany Cromwell (AUS) +7'15"9. Elisa Serné (NED) S.T.10. Haley Smith (CAN) +8'55"The temperatures have been high for much of the week but it is a cool and fresh 16°C, unusually low for spring time in the area. October 9, 2026 – 9:24 PMHello and welcome to ' live updates of the women's UCI World Gravel Championships 2026 from Nannup, Western Australia.October 9, 2026 – 9:28 PMInfo from our Australia Editor Simone Giuliani on the ground is that the course has had some overnight rain, compacting the pea gravel making the route less slippery. However, the riders will have to contend with puddles, likely not to the same extent seen at Unbound this year, but still an extra challenge for the riders. October 9, 2026 – 9:35 PMThe women face a challenging but rather short 125.6km of racing on the gravel of Western Australia, what should they be looking out for? Well, we've put together what we think will be the three things that could shape the racing...October 9, 2026 – 9:39 PMRacing is due to begin at 10:10 local time in Nannup. Roughly 30 minutes from now.October 9, 2026 – 9:48 PMFor those who may not be familiar with the gravel scene but knows road will have one name screaming out at them, that being former world gravel champion Marianne Vos. However, there are some star specialists are here with Argentina's Sofia Gomez Villafañe, home rider Nicole Frain and many more all lining up to challenge. October 9, 2026 – 9:53 PMThe course itself is extremely challenging. While it is rather short, in the 125.6km of racing there are 3180 metres of elevation gain with the climbs not allow immediate rest after the summits are they tend to plateau for a while afterwards. October 9, 2026 – 9:55 PMThe gravel is like nothing seen in European gravel racing and is unique to the area in Australia. Pea gravel is what it says on the tin, gravel that is shaped like peas. It can been incredibly slippery when dry but when wet it can be compacted down and become less notable with tyre choice being crucial. October 9, 2026 – 9:58 PMThe riders are beginning to line up on the start line in Nannup with Wendy Oosterwoud of the Netherlands wearing number one. October 9, 2026 – 10:04 PMIt is being said that this is a 'true' gravel course with 85% of the course on gravel with intense gradients and a huge amount of climbing. The chance for the specialists to finally have a pure gravel rider in the rainbow bands after road stars have dominated the first four editions. October 9, 2026 – 10:06 PMThis will be the final race in the career of South African WorldTour rider Ashleigh Moolman-Pasio despite having a cold. October 9, 2026 – 10:08 PMAustralian gravel champion and winner here for the SEVEN Gravel race in Nannup earlier in the year, Tiffany Cromwell, is another rider who will be hanging up the wheels after this race. October 9, 2026 – 10:10 PMRacing begins for the 2026 Gravel World Championships in Nannup with the Dutch team immediately up to the front. October 9, 2026 – 10:13 PMIt is a fast start on the asphalt to begin with the tiny peloton bunched together for the moment but when they hit the gravel it'll likely immediately split up. October 9, 2026 – 10:18 PMThe home nation gets the ball rolling with the first attack of the day. No-one keen on following for the time being as we are still on the asphalt with 10km until the gravel begins. October 9, 2026 – 10:19 PM12 riders down as DNFs including Germany's Romy Kaspar and the Netherlands' Riejanne Markus. October 9, 2026 – 10:23 PMBloor has a gap of just 12" on the peloton as the gravel edges closer and closer. October 9, 2026 – 10:27 PMBloor leads onto the gravel with a very wet surface and a few puddles. A couple of early twitches from the back wheel for the Australian rider. She now has 34" on the peloton. October 9, 2026 – 10:28 PMThe peloton hit the gravel and immediately things change as the pace shoots up with the Dutch crowding the front still. 5km to the first climb of the day. October 9, 2026 – 10:30 PMBloor's wheel skipping and skidding all over the place forcing her to freewheel. All the riders have only been able to recon some of the route due to some of the sections being on private property including the first climb of the day. October 9, 2026 – 10:32 PMMud is already caking the backs of the riders as the riders are on the first climb of the day now. October 9, 2026 – 10:34 PMMutsumi Hara (Japan) and Elizabeth Hermolle (Great Britain) early off the back but it is a tough start and there's a long way to go as the rain begins to fall again. October 9, 2026 – 10:40 PMThe gap goes out to a minute for Bloor who will be very happy for the moment but I imagine she would like to have some company. She rides solo for the time being. October 9, 2026 – 10:40 PMThe climb Killarney which is 5.4km of very undulating riding and an average of 3.4% but with some nasty kickers. October 9, 2026 – 10:43 PMMultiple riders now struggling to hold onto the peloton as Bloor has 1'02" on the pack.October 9, 2026 – 10:46 PMOne unexpected rider on the startlist for the elite women was Peta Mullens (Australia) who was expecting to ride the age group of 35-39 but received an email a few days ago saying she will have to race the elite due to rule changes coming into force...October 9, 2026 – 10:46 PMBloor's gap has now reduced significantly as she continues to tap out a rhythm that suits her but she now just has 30" on the chasers. October 9, 2026 – 10:47 PMThe peloton has shrunk quite a lot on this first climb with Bloor being reeled back in very soon. October 9, 2026 – 10:50 PMFormer Australian national road champion Nicole Frain is keen to see a gravel specialist take the title today...October 9, 2026 – 10:52 PMNot ideal for the Irish rider who clipped a wheel and came down. She is back riding but is now out of the back. October 9, 2026 – 10:53 PMInside 1km from the top of the Killarney climb as Bloor holds a very slender lead. October 9, 2026 – 10:55 PMBloor is caught by the Dutch led peloton that has been whittled right down on the first climb. October 9, 2026 – 10:56 PMOnto the first descent of the day now and the pace shot up to make sure they were in a good position with Vos, Sophie Wright (Great Britain) and Larissa Hartog (Netherlands) leading the way. October 9, 2026 – 10:57 PMThe sun is back out now but the gravel is very wet and slippy. October 9, 2026 – 10:59 PMOne of the big favourites for the race is trying to fix this quickly with her plugs but the sealant taking a while. She is now back riding but a long way out the back now. Similar happened in Unbound earlier this year. October 9, 2026 – 11:00 PMSome info coming from the start... The age groupers are heading out in waves now. Some were so keen to ensure a good spot in the start line that they were sitting in the ground with their bikes in their start box well over an hour before their start time.October 9, 2026 – 11:03 PMMaddy Nutt (Great Britain) was just off the back after that descent but has made it back in now. She will be relying on her huge engine and stamina to be involved in the final...October 9, 2026 – 11:05 PMThe peloton now bunches up after that descent as they build towards the first majorly hard climb of Brockwell. October 9, 2026 – 11:05 PMWright, Hartog, Cromwell and Erica Magnaldi (Italy) lead the peloton on this rolling terrain. October 9, 2026 – 11:09 PMOnto the Brockman climb with Wright and Magnaldi upping the tempo with the rain starting yet again. You won't win the race here but you can certainly lose it. October 9, 2026 – 11:10 PMThe climb is 2.5km at 8% with kicks well over 15%. October 9, 2026 – 11:11 PMKlöser has fought very well and is about 10" off the back of the lead group and is picking up riders who are losing touch. October 9, 2026 – 11:13 PMWright is ripping this peloton to bits on this climb but Klöser is about to make it back on. October 9, 2026 – 11:14 PMKlöser flies pass British duo of Nutt and Hermolle as they have to negotiate their way around one of the camera bikes that has got stuck in the mud on the gradients of Brockman. October 9, 2026 – 11:15 PMWendy Oosterwoud (Netherlands), Gravel World Series leader, has been gapped just before the hardest section. That is a big surprise. October 9, 2026 – 11:16 PMCromwell also out of the back with Denmark's Janni Spangsberg Schori losing tough as well. October 9, 2026 – 11:17 PMThe Dutch still just about have four riders in this select group with Hartog and Geerike Schreurs just holding on. October 9, 2026 – 11:21 PMSofía Gómez Villafañe (Argentina)Nicole Frain (Australia)Marianne Vos (Netherlands)Ashleigh Moolman-Pasio (South Africa) Erica Magnaldi (Italy)Elisa Serné (Netherlands)Rosa Klöser (Germany)Geerike Schreurs (Netherlands)Larissa Hartog (Netherlanda)Irina Lützelschwab (Switzerland)Haley Smith (Canada)And a few others now lead. October 9, 2026 – 11:21 PMWright did all that work on the toughest gradients but has not made the group. October 9, 2026 – 11:22 PMCromwell, Wright, Oosterwoud are now around 45" down on the leaders. October 9, 2026 – 11:23 PMThrough the feed zone now as multiple riders take on fresh bottles, bars and gels. October 9, 2026 – 11:24 PMGreat crowds around the feed area after a period on private land.October 9, 2026 – 11:24 PMOn the Adina climb now, 1.1km long at 4% average. October 9, 2026 – 11:27 PMBit of grass racing turns into mud and then some more traditional looking gravel for a very short period before returning back to the pea gravel very soon. October 9, 2026 – 11:30 PMShe has a front flat but she seems to have got it fixed pretty fast. October 9, 2026 – 11:35 PMThe gap between the lead group including Vos, Villafañe, Klöser, Moolman-Pasio and the rest have a minute on the group including Cromwell, Wright and Oosterwoud. October 9, 2026 – 11:37 PMOnto Shale climb of 800m at 6.8% which is being done very swiftly as Villafañe and Magnaldi lead the way for now. October 9, 2026 – 11:42 PMThe Shale climb appears to have favoured the chase group as the gap drops to 22", but this will be based on the motorbikes so we take that gap with a pinch of salt. October 9, 2026 – 11:43 PMAnd the gap is closing. 15" between the leaders and chasers as riders like Cromwell, Oosterwoud and Flora Johnson (Great Britain) may get back in. October 9, 2026 – 11:45 PMCromwell is leading the chasing group back to the front group as the leader's pace lulls. That was a big effort from the chasers with Oosterwoud still struggling to hold the wheel but we now have a lead group of around 16 riders. October 9, 2026 – 11:47 PMTiffany Cromwell (Australia)The Australian champion launches as soon as she re-joined the leaders to try and get clear but she is solo and the chase is on. October 9, 2026 – 11:50 PMVos tried a move but she was heavily marked. Cromwell continues to press on as the chase group starts to sit up a bit more. October 9, 2026 – 11:52 PMMagnaldi is investing a lot of energy on the front of the favourites group without dropping anyone but they stall again and allow Cromwell a bit more gap. October 9, 2026 – 11:53 PMCromwell expands her lead to 10" as the chase stalls. October 9, 2026 – 11:54 PMMarianne Vos (Netherlands)The former world champion launches for a second time to try and close Cromwell down. She is marked but it has got the rest of the group interested in chasing again. October 9, 2026 – 11:55 PMCromwell heads onto the descent, probably the longest downhill of the entire race. October 9, 2026 – 11:59 PMVos came into this race with an eye on the gravel specialists as the superstar hopes to become the first rider to take a second gravel world title...October 10, 2026 – 12:00 AMCromwell drags her advantage out to 19" and is now out of sight from the chase group as the Aussie goes solo in the Worlds, on home soil, in her final race. October 10, 2026 – 12:06 AMGeerike Schreurs (Netherlands)Ashleigh Moolman-Pasio (South Africa)The latter gets back on her feet but isn't in a rush to get going while Schreurs stays on the ground with the medics tending to both. October 10, 2026 – 12:07 AMThere was a very nasty rut that they hit and it just pushed Schreurs and Moolman-Pasio out with the former kicked to the side and into the rocks. Both look to be out of the race. October 10, 2026 – 12:08 AMMeanwhile, Cromwell has 27" gap on the chase group. October 10, 2026 – 12:11 AMA brief section of asphalt heads back onto the gravel and Cromwell has 48" on the chasers.October 10, 2026 – 12:16 AMThe Dutch have numbers but are not chasing with the Germans taking the responsibility through a very rocky and puddle filled section as Cromwell opens her gap to 1'17". October 10, 2026 – 12:18 AMNow time for the Lewana climb, 1.5km at 5.3%.October 10, 2026 – 12:19 AMA stick has got into her rear mech. She is back riding but another issue for the German after an earlier puncture. October 10, 2026 – 12:22 AMCromwell is riding really well and has 1'21" on the chasers with Magnaldi leading the chase group yet again. Klöser gets back in as well. October 10, 2026 – 12:25 AMNow that Klöser is back in the group the Germans return to the front of the chase group with Oosterwoud struggling again. October 10, 2026 – 12:27 AMNow on a very steep and technical descent on this extremely slippery pea gravel. Cromwell just overshot a hairpin and may have lost a couple of seconds.October 10, 2026 – 12:28 AMLaing and Vos have gapped the rest in the chase showing their descending skills but Cromwell has used the terrain to get her gap back to 1'17" after it dropped to 52" on the climb. October 10, 2026 – 12:33 AMCromwell now has 1'32" on the peloton as the rain pours in Western Australia.October 10, 2026 – 12:35 AMInterestingly, Villafañe is out of the back of the chase group alongside Britain's Johnson. Something must have happened as she looked so strong on the climbs. October 10, 2026 – 12:37 AMFive riders break clear of the chase group as it splits up on this latest climb. Laing, Vos, Klöser, Magnaldi and Hartog. October 10, 2026 – 12:39 AMThe chasing group of five have closed in on Cromwell rapidly on the Ellis Creek climb, the longest and hardest of the day. October 10, 2026 – 12:40 AMCromwell caught making it a lead group of six riders with 58km to go. October 10, 2026 – 12:41 AMCromwell is caught and immediately dropped with Hartog and Magnaldi. October 10, 2026 – 12:41 AMMarianne Vos (Netherlands)Rosa Klöser (Germany)October 10, 2026 – 12:44 AMGeerike Schreurs (Netherlands)October 10, 2026 – 12:45 AMHartog and Magnaldi make it back to Klöser, Laing and Vos. October 10, 2026 – 12:53 AMThe five lead riders are riding well together but they are coming up against some of the age groupers. Fortunately the tracks are wide and there's plenty of space for the pros. October 10, 2026 – 12:57 AMSome of the age group men and women are sitting in at the back of the lead group. This isn't what the pros want at all as it is distracting and can be very dangerous. October 10, 2026 – 12:59 AMKlöser just clipped the back wheel of Hartog but both stay upright. October 10, 2026 – 12:59 AMFortunately, the age groupers have been dropped by the elite women here. October 10, 2026 – 1:00 AMVos, Hartog, Magnaldi, Klöser and Laing leading the way and working well together with the rain pouring down on the riders. October 10, 2026 – 1:10 AMLaing has two World Series wins to her name with both German races going her way. Vos just seems to win almost everything she races. Klöser has had a mixed gravel year with disappointing mechanical filled Leadville 100 and Unbound but she has been superb on the road. Hartog also had a great season that started long ago in cyclocross. October 10, 2026 – 1:15 AMThe leaders are going much faster than the camera bikes on this descent and have left the bike behind. Cromwell pass them as well as she is still chasing now with teammate Frain. October 10, 2026 – 1:17 AMCromwell, Frain, Lützelschwab and Serne are getting closer to the leaders again. This could actually come together again after all that selection on the Ellis Creek climb. October 10, 2026 – 1:18 AMCromwell just being distanced from the chase group led by fellow Australian Frain. October 10, 2026 – 1:21 AMOn the Glacier climb with Frain, Serne and Lützelschwab making it back to the leaders after an amazing chase. October 10, 2026 – 1:23 AMBit of an issue for Magnaldi who had to unclip and stop on a hairpin. She has got going again but will need to spend a bit of energy. October 10, 2026 – 1:26 AMAshleigh Moolman-Pasio (South Africa)Shame to see that the South African ends her career with a DNF. October 10, 2026 – 1:29 AMHartog is now setting a hard tempo likely for Vos who is clearly one of, if not the, strongest in the race today. October 10, 2026 – 1:31 AMThe leaders are now descending down towards Nannup for the first time since the start before they start one final loop with two more climbs to come. October 10, 2026 – 1:33 AMHartog now uses her pace and gaps the rest of the group as her teammates look towards the others to chase her down. October 10, 2026 – 1:35 AMHartog is brought back as they take some fresh bottles and gels on a rare bit of asphalt. October 10, 2026 – 1:38 AMThat splits the group with Vos and Klöser being the only ones to follow. Magnaldi left to do all the chasing. October 10, 2026 – 1:38 AMMagnaldi has done a bit acceleration and has dragged the leaders back again. October 10, 2026 – 1:39 AMLaing is trying to get clear but Vos is closing her down again. October 10, 2026 – 1:47 AMSomehow Sofía Gómez Villafañe (Argentina) has chased all the way back to the front of the race again after being over 2 minutes down. October 10, 2026 – 1:48 AMFrain, Laing and Serne are struggling to follow the wheels but Villafañe is still there with a brand new wheel on her bike. October 10, 2026 – 1:48 AMSerne, Frain and Laing get back in after the pace lulls again. October 10, 2026 – 1:52 AMTiffany Cromwell (Australia)She is back and on the attack yet again. Just 900m to the final climb of the day.October 10, 2026 – 1:53 AMCromwell heads back onto the gravel and onto the final climb of Folly Farm. October 10, 2026 – 1:54 AMKlöser, Vos and Villafañe closing but now Klöser and Vos go clear of the rest. October 10, 2026 – 1:55 AMLaing is riding hard to get back to her teammate of Klöser along with Vos as they negotiate riding around the age groupers. October 10, 2026 – 1:56 AMLaing invested a lot to try and get to the leaders but Klöser and Vos now properly push clear. October 10, 2026 – 1:59 AMIt appears to be down to Vos and Klöser for this race into the final 20km.October 10, 2026 – 2:03 AMHartog makes it to Laing in the chase at 27" back from Klöser and Vos. October 10, 2026 – 2:07 AMKlöser dropped Vos at Sea Otter Europe back in late September, but this is has been a very different race and the rainbow jersey is on the line. October 10, 2026 – 2:07 AMThe sunshine has come out again after much of the race spent in the driving rain. October 10, 2026 – 2:10 AMOut front it is a Dutch rider and a German rider with the chasing duo being a Dutch rider and a German rider. The two nations have certainly dominated this race with Klöser and Vos holding 32" on Laing and Hartog.October 10, 2026 – 2:14 AMThey have taken on a short asphalt section before heading onto the final part of gravel today with the second part of the Folly climb to come. Klöser looked the strongest on the climb but Vos was able to match her. October 10, 2026 – 2:17 AMKlöser and Vos working together well since they crested the previous climb with around 35" to the chasers. October 10, 2026 – 2:21 AMInto the final 10km and the leading duo are settled into working together with it looking unlikely that anyone will re-join them. October 10, 2026 – 2:25 AMIt is now almost all downhill to Nannup with an average speed up around 27kph today. This has been a brutal day out. October 10, 2026 – 2:25 AM8km to go and the gap back to Laing and Hartog is 52".October 10, 2026 – 2:27 AMIt is easy to forget that Klöser has had a puncture on the first climb of the day, got back on then had a stick in the rear mech and got back on again. Whereas, Vos has been active but largely in the wheels always very close to the front. October 10, 2026 – 2:30 AM6km to go and they are on some very rutted section. This is the last kicker before the finish with Klöser on the front again trying to break the legs of Vos. October 10, 2026 – 2:32 AMKlöser continues to push the pace but Vos still looks good with Hartog and Laing at 1'13" back. October 10, 2026 – 2:34 AMKlöser is just riding Vos to the finish. You would think that Vos would easily win in a sprint but it has been a very long day out today.October 10, 2026 – 2:35 AMMarianne Vos (Netherlands)Rosa Klöser (Germany) can follow the Dutch star. October 10, 2026 – 2:36 AMThe German loses her front wheel as she tried to scramble onto the wheel of Vos as she attacks over the top of the final ascent. October 10, 2026 – 2:36 AMKlöser is back riding but Vos is now clear with it all downhill to the finish. October 10, 2026 – 2:37 AMThe pea gravel has dried out and we are seeing how chaotic it can be when dry. Vos is now riding away to the victory. October 10, 2026 – 2:38 AMOctober 10, 2026 – 2:39 AM1km to go for Vos as the Dutch look like they will continue their dominance in the gravel worlds as she looks like she is going to be the first rider to get a second gravel world title. October 10, 2026 – 2:40 AMMarianne Vos wins the Gravel World Championships title 2026! October 10, 2026 – 2:41 AMRosa Klöser takes an exceptional second place but the crash at the top of Tank 7 climb was one setback too much. October 10, 2026 – 2:43 AMLarissa Hartog beats Nele Laing to take the bronze medal in a day dominated by the Netherlands and Germany. October 10, 2026 – 2:49 AMMagnaldi took fifth ahead of Villafañe, Lützelschwab, Cromwell, Serne and Haley Smith rounding out the top 10. October 10, 2026 – 2:59 AMIt wasn't to be for Rosa Klöser as Marianne Vos had the power and technical skills in the important moment to get clear to take her 15 career world title across so many disciplines. October 10, 2026 – 3:12 AMThe final podium sees Vos take another rainbow jersey with Klöser in second and Hartog in third.
