'I don’t think it’s my responsibility to finance that' – Gravel pros forced to buy their own kit and fund travel to Australia for World Championships
item.author: Owen Rogers
item.content:encoded: Gravel professionals heading to the Gravel World Championships this weekend have had to pay their own way, while others have had to pay for their own national kit.The creation of the UCI Gravel World Championships, and the accompanying season-long World Series in 2022, gave the once maverick discipline a more mainstream home, but many national federations are leaving riders unsupported for the first Championships outside Europe, which take place this weekend in Nannup, Western Australia.With qualification largely coming through finishing positions in World Series events, the national teams are not strictly selected by federations, though the national bodies are able to nominate 10 riders to represent their countries, and national champions receive an automatic entry. However, even those riders selected by their nation are often going unsupported.Defending men’s world champion Florian Vermeersch, who rides on the road for UAE Team Emirates-XRG, is one of those affected. "It is a trip I have to organise myself. There is no support from the cycling federation." reported the Belgian as saying. "I race there for the national team. I'm just happy that my [road] team gives me the time and space to do this. I get equipment from my team and I pay for the flights myself, but I am willing to make that investment." understands that not only are British riders having to pay for travel and accommodation, they’re having to pay £60 for a jersey or £120 for a race suit, kit they are required to wear during the race. While that isn’t a fortune, it’s significant given many gravel elites are privateers, especially when they’re paying for their travel and accommodation. Riding for Ribble Outliers, Sophie Wright counts the British gravel title among her 2026 successes, but has paid for a large proportion of the trip herself, with her race kit on top of that. "I think it's a bit odd for us to have to buy our own kit from our national federation to represent our country. Especially as an elite professional rider, British champion, it would be nice for BC to offer some level of support," she told .Compatriot Maddy Nutt has ridden every edition of the Gravel Worlds to date and is a pure privateer, funding the trip to Western Australia from the sponsorship money she lives off."What if someone did podium and they were in the wrong kit, it wouldn’t look great for British Cycling and their sponsors. I think they’d even be at risk of disqualification, but at the same time, should it then be the athletes’ responsibility to pay for kit in order to prevent any poor reflection on BC?"I could wear kit from two years ago, but then in the photos on my social media I won’t be wearing the correct GB kit. I think it’s important that I’m in the right kit, but I don't think it's my responsibility to finance that.""Part of the reason I am not going is because of the conflicting races, but another part is the cost to go to Australia," said US gravel champion Cobe Freeburn. "It would have been very expensive and I would not have gotten any support from either USA Cycling or from Trek. I'm not surprised that only three US men are making the trip with the conflicting dates and the lack of support."In Marianne Vos and Geerike Schreurs, the Dutch have two contenders for the title and are sending staff to support them, but while they are providing their riders with accommodation, they have to pay their own way to Australia, though Schreurs will be travelling with her Specialized Off-Road trade team."We get really good support from Specialized Off-Road, so for us riders it's actually just like normal travel to a race. So it's pretty easy," she said. However, while clothing isn’t the issue it is for the British riders, the Dutch federation is providing used kit."They provide the clothing, but you have to give it back afterwards, then they use it for the next thing. So I try not to think about it too much that someone else has been wearing that kit!"The Australian, Belgian and British federations all make a distinction between Olympic and non-Olympic disciplines when providing support to riders attending World Championships, explaining the lack of support for their elite riders."As a non-Olympic discipline, the funding and resources available to support gravel differ from those available in some other areas of the sport," a British Cycling spokesperson told . "We remain committed to supporting the growth of gravel and will continue to explore the opportunities and resources available to support future editions of the event as the discipline develops."For their part, USA Cycling’s Selection Criteria document makes it clear there is no support: "FINANCIAL RESPONSIBILITY - Athletes who receive automatic invitations from the UCI or are nominated by the USA Cycling Athlete Discretionary Selection procedures are responsible for their own expense associated with this event. USA Cycling will not assume financial responsibility for any athletes." item.title: Movistar poach top under-23 talent from UAE Team Emirates-XRG
item.author: Matilda Price
item.content:encoded: UAE Team Emirates-XRG are set to lose one of their emerging young talents in 2027, with Gen Z rider Mateo Ramírez exiting the team to turn pro with Movistar.Ramírez, 20, from Ecuador, finished fourth overall at the Tour de l'Avenir this summer, just a few weeks after taking the runner-up spot at the Giro d'Italia Next Gen, and has established himself as one of the most exciting GC talents in the under-23 peloton.His contract with UAE Team Emirates-XRG Gen Z only ran to the end of this year, though, and with their WorldTour squad nearly full for 2027, there did not seem to be space for him to turn pro this winter. So instead of spending another year with the under-23 team, Ramírez found a pro contract with Movistar."I'm very happy and excited to start my WorldTour career with Movistar. It's a team with a huge history in cycling and I think it's a great fit for me, where I feel I can continue to grow, develop as a rider and gain experience," he said."I am very motivated for next year and I want to give my best, continue evolving every day and make the most of this opportunity to achieve the desired goals."Still only 20, Ramírez has already shown where his abilities lie as a top-level climber and GC specialist, and while Movistar never lack climbers, they haven't always had a serious GC contender on their books. After Enric Mas' victory at the Vuelta a España, their stock as a proper GC team has only risen, though, and Ramírez will join the likes of Cian Uijtdebroeks and Iván Romeo as their next generation of overall contenders.Ramírez is already the team's fifth signing for 2027, and he will join compatriot Jefferson Cepeda at what is set to be a strong Movistar squad for the coming seasons. "Mateo is a very talented rider with great potential for improvement," team manager Sebastián Unzue said."Our goal is to support him every step of the way in his development so that he reaches his full potential in the coming years. We are very excited about his arrival and eager to start working together."A rare 'loss' for UAE Team Emirates-XRGWhile we don't know the ins and outs of Ramírez's negotiations with UAE, and how much they wanted to keep him on their books, it's unusual to see a young talent exiting their ranks when their potential is still developing.The team have a habit of identifying and locking in talent long-term. However, this move perhaps highlights the limitations of that: even when you have the budget to sign whoever you like, you're still constrained by roster space, and even the Goliaths of the peloton can't just sign everyone. From Ramírez's side, he clearly feels ready to turn professional, and in the current era, making that step up at 20 is hardly unusual, so you can see why he sought a WorldTour contract rather than opting to spend another year at under-23 level.So while it may be an unusual tale, a young climber leaving UAE, it's a good thing to see talent spreading around the peloton. After Movistar's exploits this year at the Vuelta a España, it's exciting for them to have a future GC contender on their books.Subscribe to Cyclingnews for comprehensive race coverage of the UCI Gravel World Championships, alongside the final Monument of the season, Il Lombardia. item.title: Havertz, Isak, Dorgu … spate of injuries with national teams leaves sour taste for top clubs
item.author: John Brewin
item.content:encoded: Premier League clubs, and their European rivals, left with a long list of absentees after a gruelling international breakA four-match international break has presented a stress test. “The intensity of the squad, the athleticism of it, really, I think it’s designed for the elite,” said the Wales head coach, Craig Bellamy, on the completion of four matches in 11 days. Elite club coaches would disagree. The Nations League and the wider set of international games staged across the globe have been accompanied by a daily list of casualties, club officials viewing matches through their fingers as players pull up and gesture to the bench.Hamstring and muscle problems have been rife. Sunderland, for example, will be without Brian Brobbey, a key striker, and Dan Ballard, a defensive mainstay, because of strains picked up playing for the Netherlands and Northern Ireland respectively. Bournemouth, yet to win a Premier League match, have lost Alex Scott for up to two months. His performance for England in their 7-0 victory against Croatia won rave reviews, a young player taking his chance and outshining Luka Modric. It came at a heavy cost. A quadriceps injury that had been diagnosed pre-match worsened. “There was zero risk taken from our side,” said Thomas Tuchel. The Bournemouth coach, Marco Rose, is unlikely to see it that way.Continue reading...

item.title: 'The year where someone who's primarily a gravel racer would win – Maddy Nutt representing the specialists at the World Championships
item.author: Owen Rogers
item.content:encoded: It’s been a great year for British gravel racer Maddy Nutt. A shift in focus has seen her race some of the longest events on the calendar, racing for 24 hours and coming away with some top results.At the start of May she was the first woman home - and 17th overall - in the Traka 560, covering the 560km route in 26 hours 30 minutes. Then, later that month, she took on the 574km of Unbound XL, finishing as second woman, 34 minutes behind winner Svenja Betz. For 2026 the UCI Gravel World Championships leave Europe for the first time, with the previous four editions held in Italy twice, Belgium and the Netherlands. The 2026 event heads to Western Australia, and the town of Nannup, some 250km south of Perth, the elite women racing on Saturday, October 10, the men the following day, with the age-group events spread across the two days.At 'only' 125.6km in length, Nutt’s race will tackle less than a quarter of her two epic successes earlier in the year, so she’s been forced to alter her training to try to at least be competitive, though with a decent number victories and top five finishes in shorter races, including UCI Gravel World Series events, she’s hardly a stranger to those distances and their increased intensity."I’ve kind of switched up my racing this year to try some new stuff, and then I've kind of switched back in the second half of the season," Nutt explained when we called her before she headed to Australia. "Early season, I was prioritising doing a couple of ultra races and giving, and I actually really enjoyed them, and then I always wanted to do world champs in Australia."So at a certain point, I said I need to switch my training up because otherwise I'm not going to have the upper-end power to be able to race shorter stuff. But I've really enjoyed mixing my calendar up with different stuff, it's very different to stand on a start line knowing you're going to be racing for over 24 hours versus standing on a start line knowing you're just going to suffer for a few hours. They’re very different kinds of pain."Not a lifelong cyclist, Nutt came to cycling relatively late, and after a couple of years dabbling in road racing, she headed off the tarmac for the growing gravel scene. She raced the first edition of the Gravel Worlds in Veneto in 2022, finishing 29th behind Pauline Ferrand-Prévot, and has taken part in every edition since. Being an ever-present is part of the attraction for her to pack up her bike and head to Australia for another tilt next week."To date I’ve done four out of four and finished four out of four, I think the only other rider that has is Tiffany Cromwell, so we'll both have done five out of five, but I think she's retiring this year, so maybe if I do the one next year, I'll be the only person who's done all of them!"I feel like if I'm fit and capable of going, it's quite nice to go and do another one. I've been to Australia once before, and I loved it, so it’s an excuse to go to a place that I really enjoyed riding my bike."Professional road riders have won both men’s and women’s races in all four editions to date, but with this year’s races taking place so far from Europe and coming at the end of a long, hard season, it’s expected we’ll see fewer of them on the Nannup start line, increasing the chances of a gravel specialist winning the jerseys this year. And then there are the routes, both of which comprise well over 80% gravel, something the true off-road regulars will be well used to."This course seems like the most gravelly Gravel World Championships that we've seen, so I'm really intrigued to do a Gravel World Championships that could actually suit gravel specialists," says Nutt. "The gravel is meant to be actually quite champagne gravel, so I think it's not overly technical, but there are sections with what they describe as pea gravel, and pea gravel's super slippy, it’s like ball bearings instead of gravel."Of any year, this would be the year where someone who's primarily a gravel racer would win, I think, even if it's someone like Rosa Klöser or Gee [Geerike Schreurs] who have had that road experience as well. But someone who really prioritises this discipline and then takes the jersey would be really awesome because also we don't see the winners ever wear that jersey."While Nutt is part of clothing company Q36.5’s Off-Road Racing Expedition, that’s not quite a team, and riders arrange many of their own sponsors themselves. And with no administrative support they are responsible for running their own race programmes and expenses.That won't change for the World Championships. Whilst raced in national teams, most federations offer little to no support for the Championships, so most racers are left fending for themselves in terms of aid during the race."A privateer is the most entrepreneurial way to be a bike racer. You need to find someone to take photos of you or find someone to hand you bottles," Nutt explains. "I’ve gone to a race and not found someone to hand me bottles, then I was the only person with a hydration vest on the start line. Even just psychologically, I'm thinking I've got an extra two kilograms on my back, and that's really hard."Luckily for Nutt, one of the other Q36.5 riders lives in Perth and is injured and unable to ride, so she has one recruit to help with hydration, though Nutt is hoping some of her social media contacts can help her out too, as getting round the entire 125.6km course could prove difficult.That entrepreneurial approach to racing means managing more than just who’s handing your drinks. There are photos needed for social media, essential for sponsor exposure, booking travel and running a budget. And with no support from British Cycling for this Championships, that budget has to extend to cover the trip to Nannup for Worlds."My sponsors will pay me and then I can choose how much of that I'm putting towards race budget. Some athletes are very specific, I'm more flexible and if I really want to go to a race I'm going to spend some of my budget on it, and then what I end up with at the end of the day is my take-home salary. But I don't mind spending more money to go to races like, for example, World Champs in Australia, and then take home less money at the end of the year because I think it's an amazing opportunity."As for her set up for next Saturday’s race, Nutt is keeping it simple, riding the rigid fork Lauf Siegla. "The course isn’t technical in theory and is super hilly, so weight is something I need to think about. Tyres-wise, I’m going for the Panaracer GravelKing X1s in a 40 [millimetre]. I raced them in Finland and was super happy with them there. I might pack a set of 45s with me in case I change my mind."Subscribe to Cyclingnews for comprehensive race coverage of both the UCI Road and Gravel World Championships, alongside the final monument of the season, Il Lombardia. item.title: More than half a kilo under the UCI weight limit: Ridley's new Falcn RS has gone on a serious diet, with exotic wheels and TPU tubes as standard
item.author: thomas.wieckowski@futurenet.com (Tom Wieckowski)
item.content:encoded: Ridley has launched a brand new road bike today in the form of the Falcn RS 2.0 The Falcn model was launched back in 2023 as a bike to slot in between the Noah and Helium models and prioritised a blend of 'aero to weight'. This bike was ridden by Tour de France yellow jersey wearer Torstein Træen during this year's race. We noticed Uno-X with a different-looking Ridley bike, and now know that it was the Falcn RS 2.0. It was also spotted at the Tour Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes back in June. Ridley appears to have dropped a healthy amount of weight from the Falcn 2.0, and the frame looks similar to the 1st gen bike. The brand insists it's 'not an evolution of its predecessor, but a completely new design' The previous-gen Falcn has fairly aggressive, standard geometry. Ridley appears to have applied its more progressive modern geometry philosophy to the new Falcn now too.It sounds like dropping weight from the frame was a key concern regarding the new bike. In its lightest version, which weighs a claimed 6.2kg, it's easily within the UCI 6.8kg weight limit and still has 35mm tyre clearance. It's probably safe to assume that Traeen's Tour bike will have been bang on the 6.8kg minimum weight number. Ridley optimised the frame's carbon layup to reduce frameset weight by 12% compared to the 1st gen bike. For instance, the brake mounts are now hollow, and a new lightweight seatpost clamp has been fitted. A medium frame weighs a claimed 705 grams.Ridley says the frame has fewer 'sharper angles' and unnecessary details. In short, the Falcn was 'put on a diet' but not at the expense of lateral stiffness, which would detract from the bike's performance and ride quality. Ridley has access to its own wind tunnel facility, but we don't have much in the way of hard data for the new Falcn. What the brand does say is that aerodynamic drag has not been negatively affected. The bike's new seatpost is slimmer, in part thanks to relocating the Di2 battery to the downtube, which is said to help. The brand has also specced some interesting wheels, which we will get to.In short, it feels safe to assume that the bike is at least on a par aero-wise with the previous-gen bike, but it likely isn't going to trouble the brand's aero race bike, the Noah Fast 3.0 New geometry has been developed for the Grifn RS 2.0, which Ridley says was based on rider feedback and bike fits from the Uno-X team. The key theme is riders adopting a more forward position on the bike. To this end, Ridley has given the bike a steeper 76-degree seat tube angle across all frame sizes, which it says improves pedalling efficiency. Paired with this steeper seat tube is a longer reach and a taller stack number; the brand is aiming to create a progressive riding position to open riders' hip angles, which ties into the general move toward shorter crank lengths that is ongoing. This is along the same lines as the Felt Nexar, which launched earlier in the year.Ridley says this creates improved comfort during long efforts and also mentions the bike's lower bottom bracket to boost high-speed stability. As an example, the stack for a Medium bike is 562mm, whilst the reach is 425 mm. Quite a long number on paper, but one which is offset by the 76-degree seat tube angle. Ridley has specified some interesting wheelsets for the Falcn 2.0 stock builds, all setups will also come with TPU tubes as standard to help save weight. The top spec SRAM Red AXS build comes with exotic AX Lightness Ultra SL wheels which use a 45mm rim but weigh in at a claimed 950 grams per pair. The Ultegra Di2 build will come with Mavic Comet 50 wheels which feature carbon spokes and ceramic bearings. Finally, the Force AXS build will feature Forza Skiron RSR wheels which have a 50mm rim, 23mm internal dimension and CeramicSpeed bearings. The wheelset weighs a claimed 1197 grams. Pricing, weights and specs The Falcn RS 2.0 is available in three build options. It's also possible to configure bikes on the Ridley custom web configurator tool. Shimano Ultegra Di2 build weighs a claimed 6.8kg and costs €7,499.The SRAM Force AXS build weighs a claimed 6.65kg and comes in at €8,499.The SRAM Red AXS top spec build weighs a claimed 6.2kg and costs €12,499.

item.title: MotoGP riders divided on contentious 2027 weekend format change
Despite fractured wrist, Ion Izagirre will get dream farewell at Il Lombardia he wanted after all
item.author: James Moultrie
item.content:encoded: "A champion never gives up!" read the post on the French team's X profile, with a video of Izagirre announcing that "I didn't want to end my sports career like that, so we will see each other on Saturday at Lombardy."Izagirre had initially had his end-of-career plans wrecked by a training crash on September 30, then telling that "I'm in mourning. It's just a feeling of being hurt and demotivated, disappointed with what happened," as his final season was ended abruptly after 17 years. That was his second win of the season, also beating Quinn Simmons to the win at the GP Miguel Indurain in April.A two-time Tour de France stage winner, Vuelta a España stage winner, and GC champion from Itzulia Basque Country and the Tour de Pologne, Izagirre has been one of the best Basque riders of his generation, having turned pro in 2017. Izagirre's plans for road racing retirement don't include any full continuation as a racer, be that in gravel or any other discipline. Instead, he wants to enjoy his time with family and ride the bike as a fan. "When I hang up my wheels, that's me done for good," he said last week in an interview with . "I'll go on riding a bike out of pure pleasure, and as a fan of the sport."Cycling has given me a lot, and I think it'll help me clear my head if I need it in the future, too, by simply riding the bike. But without any need of being out there doing series, training hard and so on.Just choosing the day and the place and the time and the people I want to be with. It'll be another world."Subscribe to Cyclingnews for comprehensive race coverage of the UCI Gravel World Championships, alongside the final Monument of the season, Il Lombardia. Subscribers get unlimited access to exclusive analysis from our expert columnists, in-depth features and industry-leading tech insight. Plus, the Cyclingnews app lets you follow the action wherever you go!

item.title: Preseason Game Preview: Knicks vs. Wizards, October 8, 2026
item.author: Russell Richardson
item.content:encoded: The Knicks (0-1) host the Wizards (0-0) tonight in their first return to the court at 4 Pennsylvania Plaza since sinking the Spurs in June. New York seeks to rebound from a 97-120 loss in Philadelphia, where the starters played around 15 minutes each and Mike Brown fielded 20 players. For the Wiz, it will be their inaugural preseason game and their first chance to see how Trae Young, Anthony Davis and the top draft pick AJ Dybantsa fare against the defending champs.The last meeting between these two came March 22 at MSG. New York won 145-113. Karl-Anthony Towns posted 26 points and 16 rebounds, and Jalen Brunson added 23. Jaden Hardy led Washington with 25 points, including seven threes. The Knicks’ second-half shooting (62%) buried a Wizards team that already had 15 straight losses.Last season, Washington finished with a league-worst record of 17-65. Their defensive rating was dead last, and their offensive rating was close to it. They averaged 112.9 points and allowed 124.9. Cheer up, Wizards fans; we remember those days. The club has upgraded their talent pool with Young, Davis, and, of course, Dybantsa, but the supporting staff remains a work in progress.Dybantsa, the number one pick out of BYU, joins the Wizards’ rebuild as a 6’9” scoring wing with elite athleticism, three-level scoring, and physicality. Davis has called him a special talent, and scouts see the 19-year-old as a new messiah for the D.C. gym, with potential to be a high-usage, two-way star. That’s a tough load for a youngster to carry. Alex Sarr (second pick, 2024) has been unable to lead the team out of the desert; neither has Tre Johnson (sixth pick, 2025). The club is rich with young talent, and eventually ownership might decide that Brian Keefe is not the coach to maximize it. Now where did I leave Thibodeau’s phone number. . . .Projected Wizards starters: Young (PG), Kyshawn George (SG), Dybantsa (SF), Davis (PF), and Sarr (C). Off the bench, look for Bub Carrington, Bilal Coulibaly, Khris Middleton, and Deandre Ayton (totally forgot he landed there).New York’s starters looked sharp in limited minutes Monday before the bench lost the second half with simply atrocious shooting (finishing around 8-of-40 from deep). Mike Brown cited a lack of physicality across the board, so the ‘Zards should expect more chests and elbows. The third center position is still up for grabs, so you’ll see more of James Wiseman and Drew Eubanks off the bench.For the Knicks: Jose Alvarado is day-to-day with a knee contusion. Wizards: Alex Sarr (foot) is a game-time decision; Tristan Vukcevic (hip) and Jamir Watkins (knee) are out.The Knicks have won 12 straight regular-season games against the Wizards and 18 of the last 20 meetings. This scrimmage won’t count in the record books, but we predict the same result. Knicks by 10.I’ll miss the game because of NYC Comic Con commitments, but will catch the rerun. Look for me in the crowd if you’re at Javits; I’ll be the good-looking one. On a personal note, today’s my 20th anniversary of sobriety. ODAT. If you think you can’t stop, drop me a line. And Who: New York Knicks (0-1) vs. Washington Wizards (0-0)Date: Friday, October 5, 2026Place: Madison Square Garden, NYC, NYFollow: @ptknicksblog and bsky

item.title: Knicks Bulletin: ‘I heard that all summer’
item.author: Antonio Losada
item.content:encoded: As we patiently wait for the Knicks to host the Wiz Kiz on Thursday… …here are the latest quotables from around Tarrytown and elsewhere.On the Knicks’ lack of physicality against Philadelphia:“What bothers me is our lack of physicality throughout the ball game, and that’s the whole roster up and down. We weren’t great on the ball physically and we weren’t great with our defensive positioning physically.“The rest of the [issues are] coach talk. It’s real, but it’s coach talk that we’ll clean up watching film and all that stuff. I can’t help with the physicality. That they’ve gotta find individually, which will then turn into collectively, and that’s how you find minutes. That’s how you make the team. That’s how you contribute in a way where some of those other mistakes can be ‘OK, we’ll get better in that area and we’ll get better in this area.’“But the physicality, we have to do a better job of that from top to bottom.”On the Knicks making the game easy for the 76ers:“They got to wherever they wanted to when it comes to getting to their spots and getting good shots. We didn’t contest, we didn’t rear-view challenge and we made the game easy for them. We just turned and took a step to the rim and they came right over our back and got the offensive rebound, so that I’m concerned about and I don’t want to see happen.”On the Knicks’ poor 3-point shot selection:“I don’t care if we go 0 for 40. We took 41 and 33 of those [threes] weren’t sprays. And that’s not how we play.”On the importance of the Knicks’ preseason opener:“[I put] a good amount [of stock in this preseason game]. Obviously being results-based is not necessarily a focus, but it’s like process-driven and making sure the details are there and doing all the right things. I think those are the things you need to be concerned about, results-based not so much. Obviously we want to win but make sure the process is right.”On the second apron being used as an excuse by teams when navigating free“I heard that all summer.”On being surprised by his diminished free-agent market:“I was very surprised. I played every single game last year, played meaningful minutes the whole year. Thought I did decently or good enough in my role that I was given. But when free agency started, that wasn’t the case.”On proving himself while competing for a Knicks roster spot:“You got to prove yourself every year. I’ve been on eight teams in nine years. Every year you got to prove yourself, prove you’ve gotten better. But with this team obviously the first and second units are pretty set, I’d say. So obviously I’d have to provide a winning attitude. I’m fighting for a job right now. So any role they give me, I’d be happy to do it.”On returning to New York after previously playing for the Nets during the KD era:“I love New York. Obviously playing in Brooklyn, they’re little brother to the Knicks even if, at the time, they weren’t that good and we were really good. New York’s always a place I loved, loved winning, loved being around. When I got the call, I was like, ‘Yeah, for sure.’ ”On wanting to play for a contender:“As you know, at this point in my career, only contending teams look for me. So I’m just trying to compete for a championship. Go back to back and help them win again.”On fighting for a guaranteed roster spot:“It is what it is right now. I thought I played well enough last year to be in the running for a guaranteed job. But now I just got to show my work throughout the summer and my veteran leadership somehow.”On seeing the 76ers as a threat to the Knicks:“The Sixers can make a title run. The Sixers are the team to watch out for if you’re the New York Knicks. To me, it’s clearly about the Knicks and the Philadelphia 76ers.”On James Dolan and the lack of extensions for Leon Rose and William Wesley:“Let me put everybody in New York on blast. That damn James Dolan is getting in the way again. We have some concerns. First of all, I don’t know if it’s news or not. Where the hell is the extension for Leon Rose? Where the hell is the extension for Worldwide Wes, William Wesley? Worldwide Wes and Leon Rose ended a 53-year drought and brought a championship to New York. Where’s their extension? Where is it? That’s number one.”On the Knicks’ current contract offer to Karl-Anthony Towns:“Number two, I’m not going to tell you that Karl-Anthony Towns deserves the max. I understand that you got Brunson and Anunoby coming down the pike, but you don’t disrespect that man by cutting him short by $77 million. You don’t do that. You give him a respectable offer.”“You give him an offer that says, ‘Okay, listen. We need you to take this hit. Jalen Brunson took this hit. We need you to do it, too.’ So, it ain’t $277 million. It might be $225-$227 million, something along those lines because Brunson took a hit, too.”“You might not like it, but it’s not disrespectful. You’re saying, ‘Listen, I got the cats that you want to keep with you. I’m going to have to touch that second apron. I’m going to have to take care of your other cats.’”On the Knicks needing to take care of Jalen Brunson first:“And we know you got to, to use his term, Big Body Brunson. We got to take care of him. That’s what we can’t go to Brunson and ask him to take another cut. The man delivered the chip, and he was the superstar that did it. Okay, he is the franchise. There will be a statue erected outside of Madison Square Garden for that man one day. He erased a 53-year drought.”“Okay, we got to take care of Brunson. So, we might need y’all to take some hits, but you don’t disrespect him.”On the Knicks’ history and Towns’ value to the championship team:“For 53 years, the New York Knicks didn’t do anything but pass gas and try to tell us it was perfume. That’s what they did. They stunk up the joint year after year after year, and they finally won the chip.”“Karl-Anthony Towns has everything to do with that. I’m not telling you that he ain’t worth—first of all, he’s worth the $277 million in today’s NBA economy. It’s just that, in light of other people you have to take care of, it’s going to call for some level of sacrifice.”“But you don’t disrespect him. Karl-Anthony Towns deserves more money, and most importantly, he deserves to be respected and appreciated. And I’mma tell you why: New York has a problem.”On his concerns about James Dolan after the Knicks’ championship:“They got a problem because that same damn James Dolan that stunk up the joint for years running the New York Knicks franchise finally, after 27 years at the helm, won a chip.”“It wouldn’t surprise me at all if his mentality is, ‘All right, I delivered a chip. So now we can wait another quarter century before we win it again.’ He’s the kind of person that’ll have that kind of attitude and take that for granted.”On what he sees as a broader problem with Knicks ownership:“I’m speaking to a bigger problem. I’m speaking to a level of arrogance and dismissiveness on the part of the ownership that’s focused on the fact that he’s a champion now and not really reflecting on the years of ineptitude that he exercised running this franchise.”“And if Karl-Anthony Towns isn’t taken care of, it sends the wrong message: ‘we don’t necessarily take care of our own.’ You see what I’m saying? And that’s where it’ll lead to you not winning for the next quarter-century and beyond when you ignore your own.”“Even when the Lakers struggled, the Buss family always took care of the people who took care of them. That is what James Dolan has to remember.“Leon Rose deserves his money. Worldwide Wes deserves his money. Brunson and Anunoby deserve their money. Karl-Anthony Towns deserves the money. They clearly made money for James Dolan this past season. Yeah, they made money for him. Let’s be clear.”

item.title: The very second apron that paved the way for their title seeks to destroy the Knicks
item.author: Michael Zeno
item.content:encoded: Sports are cyclical. It’s very rare for a team to stay on top for a prolonged period of time, just the same as it’s rare for a team to stay in the doldrums for a long time. Smart organizations can keep championship windows open, and dumb organizations can keep shooting themselves in the foot, but in every sport, the bill eventually comes due. The second apron, an invention of the latest CBA, has been the NBA’s attempt to speed up the cycle. They don’t want teams like the Warriors spending five years at the top of the sport with their all-time collection of talent. They want championship windows to be shorter, but also more volatile. It’s like a conveyor belt; they want these teams to all get a taste of glory before going back to the hunt.As the current NBA champions, the Knicks are the latest team to fight a battle with the second apron. James Dolan says he does not want to exceed it, something that very few teams have done since it was introduced. They find themselves with a core that wants to be compensated as champions, but have a finite amount of money to get there. It’s easy to curse the second apron for what they’re doing to muddy up the Knicks’ title defense and beyond, but in doing that, we have to remember that the construction and reason behind this team even reaching the mountaintop was the second apron.The Minnesota Timberwolves were coming off a trip to the Western Conference Finals, but faced a massive crisis entering the 2024-25 season with their financial table. Some players needed extensions, some players had massive raises kicking in, and they were doomed to spend the season above the second apron. You can spend one year there and survive, but doing two or more years there is a death sentence. Hence, they needed to shed long-term salary.That’s how Karl-Anthony Towns became a Knick.The Boston Celtics were the type of unstoppable superteam that the league looked to avoid in 2023-24, boasting a starting five full of players who could create their own shot and hold their own defensively, an extremely rare blend. All of that was bolstered by an elite coach who maximized offensive efficiency with the three-pointer.It was expensive to keep that team together the following season, and they did it in the second apron, but they knew they had to make changes after 2024-25 to avoid dooming themselves long term with a still-young superstar in Jayson Tatum. When the Knicks took out a bruised, battered Celtics team that May, they offloaded Kristaps Porzingis and Jrue Holiday and lost Al Horford and Luke Kornet to free agency, destroying that unstoppable ceiling and paving the way for the Knicks to take their place at the top of the totem pole.The second apron unraveled the Celtics and Timberwolves, feeding a Knicks team that was excellently built and simply waited until their time to strike. Now, the Robin Hood nature of the second apron has come around to collect from the champs.Karl-Anthony Towns wants an extension. Deuce McBride wants an extension. Josh Hart (who’s less of a priority due to a team option in 2027-28) wants an extension. Jalen Brunson is due at least $290 million down the road in a future extension (and could be up to $411 million). There’s not enough room under the second apron to keep them all happy.The second apron already threw a right hook at the Knicks’ underbelly by forcing them to let go of Mitchell Robinson, but now they could come back and take McBride from them next season (or force them to trade him). The desire to keep the band together has caused a lowballing of Towns, something that is openly frustrating him in the media.And now, we’re getting reports that both he and Hart could be trade chips in February if we can’t get a deal done? What happened to all the good vibes???No matter how much “power of friendship” you have, money is the universal divider. I’m not calling Towns greedy for wanting to make more than residential losing players, Trae Young and De’Aaron Fox, but I’m also not going to call the Knicks prudish. The second apron is extremely restrictive and, at most, you can exceed it one time before its vice grips start to sink in. I’m not sure if Dolan knows that fact, but if he does, you have to be very careful with how you use it. It unfortunately seems like this will be a distraction for the Knicks in their title defense with how rigid the two sides seem to be. As much as it sucks, that’s the second apron.It steals from the rich and gives to the poor.

item.title: Knicks Bulletin: ‘Definitely heartbreaking’
item.author: Antonio Losada
item.content:encoded: The New York Knicks officially unofficially played basketball yesterday, and I can’t be happier about an opponent’s win.As Russell said in his Scenes, we’ll give them belt when it counts, but for now, all I needed was some Orange and Blue hoops in my screen.Here’s the latest from NYK world coming off Monday’s loss. Get well soon, Huk.On playing everyone available in the preseason opener:“Everybody’s been busting their behind in camp. Everybody’s good people, and it’s our first game. So I’m gonna play everybody. Twenty guys. Jose’s not playing.”On the Knicks’ lack of physicality in the preseason loss to Philadelphia:“Most of it, I was okay with (the performance). I just listed things that I saw that I know we can be better at. What bothers me is our lack of physicality throughout the ballgame, and that’s the whole roster, up and down. We weren’t great on the ball physically, and we weren’t great with our defensive positioning physically.“That I’m concerned about, and I don’t wanna see it happen (again). The rest of the stuff, it’s coach-talk. It’s real, but it’s coach-talk that we’ll clean up watching film and all that stuff. I can’t help with the physicality. That they got to find it individually, which will then turn into collectively. That’s how you find minutes. That’s how you make the team. That’s how you contribute.”On evaluating the Knicks’ options at center:“I think just it’s just kind of gut feel. And then we’ll look at production because they’re gonna probably give us different levels of protection in different areas. Tony is just a really smart guy that has a great feel for the game, and when you watch him play, they’re not necessarily sexy, but he’s extremely efficient, and then there are times when it’s like, ‘Oh, my God, he kicked our ass [in the past].“When you look at Wiseman, he’s younger, he’s a little more raw, he’s a vertical threat. He’s one of the best runners I’ve been around. You can see and feel his length and his athleticism and his potential.“Then when you look at Drew, just a toughness about him, and you know what you’re gonna get, not tonight, but every fricking night that you go out there, ’cause he’s got a great feel, a great sense of toughness about him, and again, he’s not afraid to do anything against anybody, and his belief is at a pretty high level.“So they’ll all initially bring something a little bit different, and we’ll just see, at the end of the day, if any of them, in terms of the center spot, fit well enough to be on our team.”On Mikal Bridges attacking the rim:“It’s great. He’s long, athletic and smart. He can finish at the rim. He’s capable of playing off of two feet and making a spray because he has a tremendous feel for the game.”On creating more offensive opportunities for OG Anunoby:“We have to try and put him in those positions a bit more, but he also has to have a good feel of what he wants and get to his spots. With him being in the system for a year, he’s got a better feel. … We also have a better feel on how to use him. I don’t call a lot of plays, and now he can find the small areas where he can be aggressive offensively. … His natural ability, especially with how hard he works, is showing.”On wishing Ariel Hukporti a speedy recovery:“We hope Ariel — whatever is wrong with him — he has a speedy recovery and he’s back on the floor. You hate to see anybody go down with an injury, but especially somebody who is a caliber person who Ariel is.”On the 76ers’ roster and their status as an Eastern Conference contender:“You look at their roster, man, it’s just loaded: multiple-time All-Star, multiple-time All-Star, multiple-time All-Star, MVP candidate, MVP candidate, MVP candidate. I remember back in the day, Pop said — when I was an assistant for him — there is a change from having two All-Stars on your team to having three. He brought it to our attention as a staff. He was like, you made at least three NBA All-Stars, and not just one-offs, but perennial All-Stars to go win a championship.“And this is when we were going against Kobe [Bryant] and Shaq[uille O’Neal] and their [Lakers] team and all that.“You look at this [Philly] team here, and they’ve got as many All-Stars or guys of that nature as they had in Miami when LeBron was down there. So they’re definitely a deep team, a talented team. Nick Nurse does a phenomenal job. He’s a championship-level coach, and they’re definitely going to be one of the teams that are contending in the East.“In my opinion, it just got harder for everybody with the team that they assembled here.”On LeBron James reaching his 24th NBA season:“The first thing, I guess like year 24 is insane. It’s unheard of. It’s not human. People talk about Wemby being not human because of what he can do for his size. You got to throw LeBron in that category because of his durability and still doing it at the age that he has at a high level. It’s amazing to watch, but if there’s anybody that’s going to do it, he’s going to do it because even when he was young, he was really diligent about taking care of his body and he was not afraid to ask the vets, like Zydrunas Ilgauskas, who was one of the best in terms of taking care of his body, he was not afraid to ask him what he does daily and then follow his lead. So just an amazing, amazing run for one of the all-time greats.”On the championship-level upgrade to his travel toiletries kit:“Something has changed: This is kind of cool. So, our equipment guys are great, Kyle, Steve, Will, shout out to them. One of the best in the league, and they give me a toothbrush and toothpaste, mouthwash, and lotion, and all that. And they put it in my locker area, and they usually just carry it in a paper bag or a plastic bag.“[Now] they put it in one of those travel things. And they set it really nice on my desk, and I go in there today, and these freaking guys, they made a travel case. Like this is where my lotion is. This is where the Kleenex goes. The two travel Listerines, the deodorant, and Sensodyne toothpaste in the back.“And, it’s foam. It’s in a case, and not only that, you can’t see it, but right here, it says lotion. Right here, it says deodorant. So this is what championship level coaches get, right? I guarantee Nick [Nurse] has this s–t, too.”On what he wants from a Knicks contract extension:“Simply put, I want to do something that can keep the team together and that can work with the Knicks, but also values me. And none of those things have come close to happening.”On wanting to be paid according to his value after winning a championship and not making concessions:“No s–t, Sherlock. I just got a championship, you thought it’d be pretty easy… unless you guys think I got anything else to prove?”On the outlook for reaching an extension before the regular season:“It don’t look good. I mean in my experience, you just appreciate the moments right now and let it go where it goes.”On how he is handling the lack of an extension:On the Knicks’ preseason opener:“It’s a good first step. Not a great first step, but as long as we’re making strides in the right direction, it’s something to be happy about. Still a lot for us to learn and be better at early”On Ariel Hukporti’s injury:“Definitely heartbreaking. When I came back in the locker room, I went to go check on him. Sad to see. Obviously, we’ll pray for him.”On his first game with the“It felt good just trying to contribute to the team”On Karl-Anthony Towns and Josh Hart potentially becoming trade candidates if they remain unsigned:“Josh Hart has already hinted that, as this gets closer to February, which is around the trade deadline. “The temperature could rise if Karl-Anthony Towns and Hart himself are not extended. So far, these sides are not close.”

item.title: Thrown in with Giggs and Beckham: how Manchester United tried to get Billy Kenny
item.author: Billy Kenny
item.content:encoded: Former Everton midfielder, known as the ‘Goodison Gazza’, recalls being made to feel special by Alex Ferguson in this autobiography extract “So this is the scouser ya been goin’ on aboot then …” My face turned Manchester United red. Scanning the room full of smiles and staring eyes, I identified the mystery Scottish voice as the man who’d just become the first player to score more than 20 league goals for the club since George Best in the 1960s. “Good answer,” replied Brian McClair after following up on my smile and nod by asking whether I supported Everton or Liverpool. “Ye’ll dee well ’ere laddie.”Brian Kidd had just introduced me to the Man United first team by silencing the room to draw attention to my presence. “Lads, this is Billy from up the road,” he said. I was still starstruck from seeing all these famous faces as my chauffeur for the day, Eric Harrison, pulled up in the car park at The Cliff a few minutes earlier. Paul McGrath. Mark Hughes. Bryan Robson. Kevin Moran. Norman Whiteside. I ticked them all off in my head. Thank fuck I was developing an ear for everyday Glaswegian because after a bit of piss-taking from the first-teamers about being a scouser, I found myself standing in an office at the end of a short and narrow corridor, shaking hands with another one.Continue reading...

item.title: Eastern Spain braces for torrential rain and flooding
item.author: Megan Davies and James Michelin for MetDesk
item.content:encoded: Up to 300mm of rain could fall in places, while extreme downpours bring landslides and deaths in NepalTorrential rain and potentially damaging flooding are forecast in eastern Spain over the coming days, as cold upper air moves over the warm, humid surface air of the Mediterranean Sea, fuelling violent, slow-moving thunderstorms near Spain’s east coast. The weather pattern, known as a Dana, occurs most often in autumn.Models show more than 100mm of rain could fall across the region on Friday, with 200-300mm possible in some areas. Cities including Valencia and Castelló de la Plana, are most at risk. Valencia has experienced several damaging floods in recent years. Catalonia has now put three towns under lockdown and Valencia has shut schools for nearly half a million children.Continue reading...

item.title: Manchester United report seventh straight annual loss and sell fans £125 grass clumps
item.author: Matt Hughes
item.content:encoded: Net loss of £43m for year ended 30 June 2026Revenue hits record £677.6m and forecast to growManchester United have reported an annual loss for the seventh ­successive year, taking the club’s combined losses to £444m since 2019.The financial results were released as it emerged United are raising revenue by selling small clumps of grass from the Old Trafford pitch to supporters. United relaid the playing surface for the first time in 14 years this summer and an email to fans has offered them the chance to buy 7cm x 7cm clumps of turf for £125.Continue reading...

item.title: Slip sliding away: football season-ticket holders fear falling down pecking order
item.author: Paul MacInnes
item.content:encoded: It is a symbol of the connection between the fanbase and club, but there is a growing fear executives would prefer stadiums full of one-off touristsThe document known as “the oldest football season ticket in the world” promises its bearer access to every Burnley home game of the 1884-85 season. It is a ticket that predates the Football League by four years, with all the fixtures played against east Lancashire neighbours. All the same, the legend on the ticket carries a stern warning: “This card is not transferable. Any member violating this rule will be at once expelled from the club.”For Burnley 1884 read Manchester United 2026. While the oldest remaining season ticket is preserved safely at Turf Moor, at Old Trafford 685 season tickets were voided this summer after a club investigation found evidence of their having been resold on the secondary market. United said such practices “undermine fair access to tickets for genuine supporters and have no place at Manchester United”. United fan groups again protested against the actions of the club’s ownership, claiming: “The way you treat us is a disgrace.”Continue reading...

item.author: Guardian Staff

Plus letters from and For this small compromise from the billionaires (who will still play the money markets and profit from others’ hard labour), the government could offer to reduce employers’ taxation costs by increasing the point at which low-paid people pay tax. Perhaps it could reduce national insurance payments for low-paid people, both employee and employer, thereby stopping the farce of the government paying income support to those on low incomes and then increasing taxation to fund it.Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action
item.author: Guardian sport
item.content:encoded: Liverpool look stronger at the back, youngsters shine for Brighton and Brentford, and James Trafford makes his England case with LeedsIn the week that 16-year-old Max Dowman has been thrust into the spotlight, it was another teenager who gave us a glimpse of the future in Brighton’s impressive win over Arsenal. Charalampos Kostoulas – nicknamed ‘Babis’ in his homeland, in homage to former Argentina striker Gabriel Batistuta – has already started twice as many Premier League games as he did in his first season in English football, when he was a backup for Danny Welbeck. The 19-year-old repaid Fabian Hürzeler’s faith in him against the reigning champions. Despite his tender years, Kostoulas already possesses the physical attributes to mix it with the best. He caused Gabriel Magalhães and company problems all afternoon, capping it off with a brilliant goal from 25 yards, his third in eight days. “We always knew that he’s capable of scoring goals out of nowhere,” said Hürzeler. “He just has this intrinsic motivation of really improving every day. He gets more and more professional, he understands the demands from the Premier League more, he understands our demands.” Continue reading...

item.title: Carrick disputes Cunha’s claim that Manchester United lacked energy in Fulham draw
item.author: David Hytner at Craven Cottage
item.content:encoded: Michael Carrick insists team ‘kept pushing’ for levellerMatheus Cunha: ‘Fulham put in more energy than us’Michael Carrick rejected the suggestion that his Manchester United players lacked physical fitness after they snatched a last-gasp 1-1 draw at Fulham on Sunday. The statistics showed the home side ran a collective 6.6km more than United, whose goalscorer in the 89th minute – Matheus Cunha – was critical of his team’s efforts.United were poor after the restart at 0-0, leading up to a disastrous Lisandro Martínez own goal in the 63rd minute, with Cunha saying they had to give more. “In the beginning of the second half, Fulham put in more energy than us and we cannot accept this,” Cunha said.Continue reading...

item.title: Manchester United’s engine room runs out of steam as fans voice frustration | Jacob Steinberg
item.author: Jacob Steinberg at Craven Cottage
item.content:encoded: Carrick’s side were short on inspiration, despite the summer spend in midfield, and the lack of quality in the final third was starkOne of the more damning aspects of Manchester United’s tortured rebuild is their inability to multitask. So much money has been frittered away, pushing United into the ridiculous position of going one position at a time each summer. Last year was all about the attack and the recent window was about central midfield, even though the options at full-back do not look strong enough to cope with a season back in the Champions League.United remain a listless, drifting operation. The ownership is reviled and the fanbase is becoming increasingly mutinous. It was not just Gary Neville seeing red as he commentated on United’s dismal efforts away to winless Fulham. There was an ominous shift in the mood in the away end at Craven Cottage, summed up by the boos that greeted Michael Carrick substituting Kobbie Mainoo with 10 minutes to go.Continue reading...
